bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起閼逢困敦，盡著雍困敦，凡二十五年。

translations.literal: From Efayin Gundun through Zhuayong Gundun; twenty-five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Efayin Gundun through Zhuayong Gundun—twenty-five years in all.

sentences.zh: 1楚懷王亡歸。

translations.literal: 1. King Huai of Chu fled to return home.
translations.idiomatic: 1. King Huai of Chu fled homeward.

sentences.zh: 秦人覺之，遮楚道。

translations.literal: The men of Qin discovered it and blocked the Chu road.
translations.idiomatic: Qin discovered it and blocked the roads to Chu.

sentences.zh: 懷王從間道走趙。

translations.literal: King Huai went by a secret path toward Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai took a bypath and fled toward Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙主父在代，趙人不敢受。

translations.literal: The Lord-Father of Zhao was at Dai; the Zhao people did not dare receive him.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord-Father of Zhao was in Dai; the Zhao people dared not shelter him.

sentences.zh: 懷王將走魏，秦人追及之，以歸。

translations.literal: King Huai was about to go to Wei; the men of Qin overtook him and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai was about to flee to Wei when Qin pursuers caught him and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 1楚懷王發病，薨於秦，秦人歸其喪。

translations.literal: 1. King Huai of Chu fell ill, died in Qin; the men of Qin returned his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: 1. King Huai of Chu fell ill and died in Qin; Qin sent his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 楚人皆憐之，如悲親戚。

translations.literal: The Chu people all pitied him, as if mourning kin.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu people pitied him as they would mourn their own kin.

sentences.zh: 諸侯由是不直秦。

translations.literal: From this the feudal lords did not regard Qin as upright.
translations.idiomatic: From this the feudal lords ceased to regard Qin as righteous.

sentences.zh: 2齊、韓、魏、趙、宋同擊秦，至鹽氏而還。

translations.literal: 2. Qi, Han, Wei, Zhao, and Song together attacked Qin, reached Yanshi, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Qi, Han, Wei, Zhao, and Song jointly attacked Qin, reached Yanshi, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秦與韓武遂、與魏封陵以和。

translations.literal: Qin made peace with Han at Wusui and with Wei at Fengling.
translations.idiomatic: Qin made peace with Han at Wusui and with Wei at Fengling.

sentences.zh: 3趙主父行新地，遂出代；

translations.literal: 3. The Lord-Father of Zhao toured the new lands, then left Dai;
translations.idiomatic: 3. The Lord-Father of Zhao toured the new territories, then left Dai;

sentences.zh: 西遇樓煩王於西河而致其兵。

translations.literal: going west he met the king of Loufan at Xihe and took over his troops.
translations.idiomatic: going west he met the king of Loufan on the Xi River and absorbed his army.

sentences.zh: 4魏襄王薨，子昭王〔遫〕立<ref>子昭王〔遫〕立據《史記·魏世家》索隱引《世本》補。

translations.literal: 4. King Xiang of Wei died; his son King Zhao [Su] succeeded<ref>King Zhao [Su] succeeded—"Su" supplemented per Suoyin to the "House of Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian citing the Shiben.
translations.idiomatic: 4. King Xiang of Wei died; his son King Zhao [Su] succeeded<ref>"Su" for King Zhao's succession is added from Suoyin to "House of Wei" citing the Shiben.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 5韓襄王薨，子釐王咎立。

translations.literal: 5. King Xiang of Han died; his son King Xi Jiu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: 5. King Xiang of Han died; his son King Xi Jiu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 1秦尉錯伐魏襄城。

translations.literal: 1. Wei Cuo, Qin Vice-Marshal, attacked Xiangcheng of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Qin Vice-Marshal Wei Cuo attacked Xiangcheng in Wei.

sentences.zh: 2趙主父與齊、燕共滅中山，遷其王於膚施。

translations.literal: 2. The Lord-Father of Zhao with Qi and Yan jointly destroyed Zhongshan and moved its king to Fushi.
translations.idiomatic: 2. The Lord-Father of Zhao, with Qi and Yan, destroyed Zhongshan and relocated its king to Fushi.

sentences.zh: 歸，行賞，大赦，置酒，酺五日。

translations.literal: On his return he distributed rewards, proclaimed a general amnesty, set out wine, and held communal feasting for five days.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he rewarded his men, proclaimed a general amnesty, set out wine, and held five days of public revelry.

sentences.zh: 3趙主父封其長子章於代，號曰安陽君。

translations.literal: 3. The Lord-Father of Zhao enfeoffed his eldest son Zhang at Dai, styling him Lord Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: 3. The Lord-Father enfeoffed his eldest son Zhang in Dai as Lord Anyang.

sentences.zh: 安陽君素侈，心不服其弟。

translations.literal: Lord Anyang had always been extravagant; in his heart he did not submit to his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Anyang had long been extravagant and inwardly refused to bow to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 主父使田不禮相之。

translations.literal: The Lord-Father sent Tian Buli to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord-Father appointed Tian Buli as his chief minister.

sentences.zh: 李兌謂肥義曰：「公子章強壯而志驕，黨眾而欲大，田不禮忍殺而驕，二人相得，必有陰謀。

translations.literal: Li Dui said to Fei Yi: "Lord Zhang is strong and his will is proud; his faction is numerous and his desires are great; Tian Buli is cruel in killing and proud—the two suit each other; there must be a secret plot.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dui said to Fei Yi: "Lord Zhang is strong-bodied and proud in ambition; his faction is large and his desires vast; Tian Buli is ruthless and murderous, proud in temper—the two suit each other. There must be a secret plot afoot.

sentences.zh: 夫小人有欲，輕慮淺謀，徒見其利，不顧其害，難必不久矣。

translations.literal: When petty men have desires, they lightly consider and shallowly plan, seeing only the profit and not the harm—calamity cannot be long in coming.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men with desires think lightly and plan shallowly; they see only gain, never harm—disaster cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 子任重而勢大，亂之所始而禍之所集也。

translations.literal: Your burden is heavy and your power is great—you are where disorder begins and where calamity gathers.
translations.idiomatic: Your burden is heavy and your power great—you stand where disorder begins and calamity gathers.

sentences.zh: 子奚不稱疾毋出而傳政於公子成，毋為禍梯，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Why do you not plead illness, stay within, and transfer government to Lord Cheng—do not be a ladder for calamity; would that not do?
translations.idiomatic: Why not plead illness, stay indoors, and hand power to Lord Cheng? Do not be the ladder by which disaster climbs—is that not better?

sentences.zh: 」肥義曰：「昔者主父以王屬義也，曰：『毋變而度，毋易而慮，堅守一心，以歿而世。

translations.literal: " Fei Yi said: "Formerly the Lord-Father entrusted the king to Yi, saying: 'Do not change your measure; do not alter your deliberations; firmly keep one heart, until death and for generations.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei Yi said: "Once the Lord-Father entrusted the king to me, saying: 'Do not change your standard; do not shift your plans; hold one heart steadfast, unto death and for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 』義再拜受命而籍之。

translations.literal: ' Yi twice bowed, received the charge, and recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: ' I bowed twice, accepted the charge, and set it down in writing.

sentences.zh: 今畏不禮之難而忘吾籍，變孰大焉！

translations.literal: Now, fearing Buli's peril and forgetting my record—what change could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Now, fearing Buli's threat and forgetting what I recorded—what betrayal could be greater?

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『死者復生，生者不愧。

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'If the dead could live again, the living would have no shame.
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says: 'If the dead could rise again, the living would feel no shame.

sentences.zh: 』吾欲全吾言，安得全吾身乎！

translations.literal: ' I wish to keep my words whole—how can I keep my person whole!
translations.idiomatic: ' I wish to keep my word whole—how can I keep my body whole?

sentences.zh: 子則有賜而忠我矣。

translations.literal: You have shown kindness and been loyal to me.
translations.idiomatic: You have done me a kindness and been loyal to me.

sentences.zh: 雖然，吾言已在前矣，終不敢失！

translations.literal: Even so, my words are already set forth—I ultimately dare not fail them!
translations.idiomatic: Even so, my pledge stands already—I dare not break it in the end!

sentences.zh: 」李兌曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " Li Dui said: "Agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Dui said: "Very well.

sentences.zh: 子勉之矣！

translations.literal: Press on, sir!
translations.idiomatic: Do your utmost, sir!

sentences.zh: 吾見子已今年耳。

translations.literal: I shall see you only within this year.
translations.idiomatic: I expect to see you only within this year.

sentences.zh: 」涕泣而出。

translations.literal: " He wept as he went out.
translations.idiomatic: " He left in tears.

sentences.zh: 李兌數見公子成以備田不禮。

translations.literal: Li Dui repeatedly visited Lord Cheng to guard against Tian Buli.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dui repeatedly visited Lord Cheng to prepare against Tian Buli.

sentences.zh: 肥義謂信期曰：「公子章與田不禮聲善而實惡，內得主而外為暴，矯令以擅一旦之命，不難為也。

translations.literal: Fei Yi said to Xin Qi: "Lord Zhang and Tian Buli sound friendly but are in truth hostile; inwardly they have a master, outwardly they act violently—forging orders to seize command for a day is not hard for them.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi said to Xin Qi: "Lord Zhang and Tian Buli sound cordial but are in truth at odds; they have backing within and act violently without—forging orders to seize power for a day would not be hard for them.

sentences.zh: 今吾憂之，夜而忘寐，饑而忘食，盜出入不可以不備<ref>盜出入不可以不備章校「十二行本無『以』字；

translations.literal: Now I worry over this—at night I forget sleep, when hungry I forget food; thieves coming and going cannot go unguarded<ref>Thieves coming and going cannot go unguarded—Zhang's collation: the twelve-line edition lacks the character "yi";
translations.idiomatic: I worry so that at night I forget sleep and when hungry I forget food; thieves entering and leaving must be guarded against<ref>"must be guarded against"—Zhang's collation: the twelve-line edition lacks "yi";

sentences.zh: 乙十一行本同。

translations.literal: the Y eleven-line edition agrees.
translations.idiomatic: the Y eleven-line edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 」《史記·趙世家》同，但不刪亦可。

translations.literal: " The "House of Zhao" in the Records of the Grand Historian agrees; yet not deleting it is also acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: " The "House of Zhao" in Records of the Grand Historian agrees; leaving the character in is also acceptable.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 自今以來，有召王者必見吾面，我將以身先之。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever the king is summoned, he must see my face first; I will put my body before him.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whoever summons the king must pass me first; I will put my body in the way.

sentences.zh: 無故而後王可入也。

translations.literal: Only if there is no cause may the king enter afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Only if there is no cause for alarm may the king enter after.

sentences.zh: 」信期曰：「善。

translations.literal: " Xin Qi said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin Qi said: "Well said.

sentences.zh: 主父使惠文王朝群臣而自從旁窺之，見其長子累然也，反北面為臣。

translations.literal: The Lord-Father had King Huiwen attend court before the ministers while he himself watched from the side; he saw his eldest son worn and abject, turning north to serve as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord-Father had King Huiwen hold court before the ministers while he watched from the side; he saw his eldest son worn down, bowing north as a subject.

sentences.zh: 詘於其弟，心憐之，於是乃欲分趙而王公子章於代，計未決而輟。

translations.literal: Subdued before his younger brother, his heart pitied him; thereupon he wished to divide Zhao and make Lord Zhang king in Dai—the plan was not settled and was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Humbled before his younger brother, he pitied him in his heart and wished to split Zhao and make Lord Zhang king in Dai—but the plan was never settled and was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 主父及王游沙丘，異宮，公子章、田不禮以其徒作亂，詐以主父令召王。

translations.literal: The Lord-Father and the king were touring Sand Hill in separate palaces; Lord Zhang and Tian Buli with their followers raised a revolt, falsely using the Lord-Father's order to summon the king.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord-Father and the king were at Sand Hill in separate palaces; Lord Zhang and Tian Buli raised a revolt with their followers, forging the Lord-Father's order to summon the king.

sentences.zh: 肥義先入，殺之。

translations.literal: Fei Yi entered first and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi went in first and killed him.

sentences.zh: 高信即與王戰。

translations.literal: Gao Xin immediately fought with the king.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xin immediately fought at the king's side.

sentences.zh: 公子成與李兌自國至，乃起四邑之兵入距難，殺公子章及田不禮，滅其黨。

translations.literal: Lord Cheng and Li Dui came from the capital, then raised troops from four districts to enter and repel the trouble, killing Lord Zhang and Tian Buli and exterminating their faction.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cheng and Li Dui came from the capital, raised troops from four districts, marched in to suppress the revolt, killed Lord Zhang and Tian Buli, and wiped out their faction.

sentences.zh: 公子成為相，號安平君；

translations.literal: Lord Cheng became chancellor, styled Lord of Anping;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cheng became chancellor, styled Lord of Anping;

sentences.zh: 李兌為司寇。

translations.literal: Li Dui became Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dui became Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 是時惠文王少，成、兌專政。

translations.literal: At this time King Huiwen was young; Cheng and Dui held sole power.
translations.idiomatic: King Huiwen was still young; Cheng and Dui held sole power.

sentences.zh: 公子章之敗也，往走主父，主父開之。

translations.literal: When Lord Zhang was defeated, he fled to the Lord-Father; the Lord-Father opened to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Zhang was defeated, he fled to the Lord-Father, who admitted him.

sentences.zh: 成、兌因圍主父〔宮〕<ref>成兌因圍主父〔宮〕章校「十二行本『父』下有『宮』字；

translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Dui then besieged the Lord-Father's [palace]<ref>"palace" after "Father"—Zhang's collation: the twelve-line edition has "palace";

translations.literal: the Y eleven-line edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: the Y eleven-line edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 孔本同；

translations.literal: Kong's edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: Kong's edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 張校同；

translations.literal: Zhang's collation agrees;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's collation agrees;

sentences.zh: 退齋校同。

translations.literal: Tuizhai's collation agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Tuizhai's collation agrees.

sentences.zh: 」《史記·趙世家》同，據補。

translations.literal: " The "House of Zhao" in the Records of the Grand Historian agrees; supplemented accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " The "House of Zhao" in Records of the Grand Historian agrees; "palace" added accordingly.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 公子章死，成、兌謀曰：「以章故，圍主父；

translations.literal: Lord Zhang died; Cheng and Dui plotted, saying: "Because of Zhang we besieged the Lord-Father;
translations.idiomatic: After Lord Zhang died, Cheng and Dui plotted: "We besieged the Lord-Father on Zhang's account;

sentences.zh: 即解兵，吾屬夷矣！

translations.literal: if we now disband the troops, our clans will be exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: if we disband now, our clans will be wiped out!

sentences.zh: 」乃遂圍之，令：「宮中人後出者夷！

translations.literal: " They then continued the siege and ordered: "Whoever leaves the palace last shall be exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: " They kept the siege and ordered: "Whoever leaves the palace last shall be killed!

sentences.zh: 」宮中人悉出。

translations.literal: " Everyone in the palace came out.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone in the palace came out.

sentences.zh: 主父欲出不得，又不得食，探雀鷇而食之。

translations.literal: The Lord-Father wished to go out but could not; he also could not obtain food, and pulled fledglings from nests to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord-Father could neither get out nor get food; he pulled nestlings from the eaves and ate them.

sentences.zh: 三月餘，餓死沙丘宮。

translations.literal: After more than three months he starved to death in Sand Hill Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After more than three months he starved to death in Sand Hill Palace.

sentences.zh: 主父定死，乃發喪赴諸侯。

translations.literal: Once the Lord-Father's death was fixed, they sent out mourning to the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Once his death was certain, they announced mourning to the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 主父初以長子章為太子，後得吳娃，愛之，為不出者數歲。

translations.literal: At first the Lord-Father had made his eldest son Zhang crown prince; later he obtained the Wu girl, loved her, and for several years did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Lord-Father had made his eldest son Zhang crown prince; later he won the Wu girl, loved her, and for years scarcely left his chambers.

sentences.zh: 生子何，乃廢太子章而立之。

translations.literal: She bore a son, He; he then deposed Crown Prince Zhang and established him.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son, He; he deposed Zhang and made He crown prince.

sentences.zh: 吳娃死，愛馳；

translations.literal: When the Wu girl died, his love ran wild;
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu girl died, his passion waned;

sentences.zh: 憐故太子，欲兩王之，猶豫未決，故亂起。

translations.literal: pitying the former crown prince, he wished to make both kings; he hesitated and could not decide—therefore disorder arose.
translations.idiomatic: pitying the former crown prince, he wished to split the realm between the two; he hesitated and could not decide—so the revolt broke out.

sentences.zh: 4秦樓緩免相，魏冉代之。

translations.literal: 4. Lou Yuan of Qin was removed as chancellor; Wei Ran replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: 4. Qin dismissed Lou Yuan as chancellor; Wei Ran replaced him.

sentences.zh: 1秦敗魏師于解。

translations.literal: 1. Qin defeated the Wei army at Xie.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Qin defeated the Wei army at Xie.

sentences.zh: 1韓公孫喜、魏人伐秦。

translations.literal: 1. Gongsun Xi of Han and men of Wei attacked Qin.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Gongsun Xi of Han and Wei forces attacked Qin.

sentences.zh: 穰侯薦左更白起於秦王以代向壽將兵，敗魏師、韓師於伊闕，斬首二十四萬級，虜公孫喜，拔五城。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Rang recommended Left Senior Bai Qi to the king of Qin to replace Xiang Shou in command of the army; he defeated the Wei and Han armies at Yique, beheaded two hundred forty thousand, captured Gongsun Xi, and took five cities.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Rang recommended Left Senior Bai Qi to the king of Qin to replace Xiang Shou as commander; Bai Qi routed the Wei and Han armies at Yique, took two hundred forty thousand heads, captured Gongsun Xi, and seized five cities.

sentences.zh: 秦王以白起為國尉。

translations.literal: The king of Qin made Bai Qi National Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qin appointed Bai Qi National Marshal.

sentences.zh: 2秦王遺楚王書曰：「楚倍秦，秦且率諸侯伐楚，願王之飭士卒，得一樂戰！

translations.literal: 2. The king of Qin sent a letter to the king of Chu, saying: "Chu has turned against Qin; Qin is about to lead the feudal lords to attack Chu. I wish Your Majesty to drill your soldiers so we may have a joyous battle!
translations.idiomatic: 2. The king of Qin wrote the king of Chu: "Chu has betrayed Qin; Qin will soon lead the feudal lords against Chu. Drill your troops, Majesty—we may yet enjoy a good fight!

sentences.zh: 」楚王患之，乃復與秦和親。

translations.literal: " The king of Chu was troubled by this and thereupon renewed kinship peace with Qin.
translations.idiomatic: " The king of Chu was alarmed and renewed a marriage alliance with Qin.

sentences.zh: 1楚襄王迎婦於秦。

translations.literal: 1. King Xiang of Chu welcomed a bride from Qin.
translations.idiomatic: 1. King Xiang of Chu took a bride from Qin.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：甚哉秦之無道也，殺其父而劫其子；

translations.literal: :: Master Guang said: How utterly lawless is Qin—killing a father and coercing the son;
translations.idiomatic: :: Master Guang said: How lawless Qin is—killing the father and holding the son hostage;

sentences.zh: 楚之不競也，忍其父而婚其仇！

translations.literal: how unable to contend is Chu—enduring its father's death and marrying its enemy!
translations.idiomatic: how unable to contend is Chu—bearing its father's death and wedding its enemy!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 楚之君誠得其道，臣誠得其人，秦雖強，烏得陵之哉！

translations.literal: Had the ruler of Chu truly possessed the Way and his ministers truly possessed the men, though Qin were strong—how could it have bullied Chu!
translations.idiomatic: Had the ruler of Chu truly held the Way and his ministers truly held worthy men, however strong Qin was—how could it have lorded over Chu!

sentences.zh: 善乎荀卿論之曰：「夫道，善用之則百里之地可以獨立，不善用之則楚六千里而為仇人役。

translations.literal: Well said is Xun Qing's discussion: "The Way—well used, a hundred-li domain can stand alone; ill used, Chu's six thousand li serve an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Qing put it well: "The Way—well used, a domain of a hundred li can stand alone; ill used, Chu's six thousand li become slaves to an enemy.

sentences.zh: 」故人主不務得道而廣有其勢，是其所以危也。

translations.literal: " Therefore when a lord does not strive for the Way but broadly possesses mere power—that is why he is in peril.
translations.idiomatic: " When a ruler does not pursue the Way but only amasses power—that is why he falls into peril.

sentences.zh: 2秦魏冉謝病免，以客卿燭壽為丞相。

translations.literal: 2. Wei Ran of Qin pleaded illness and was dismissed; the guest-minister Zhu Shou was made chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Wei Ran of Qin resigned on grounds of illness; the guest-minister Zhu Shou became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 1秦伐韓，拔宛。

translations.literal: 1. Qin attacked Han and took Wan.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Qin attacked Han and seized Wan.

sentences.zh: 2秦燭壽免。

translations.literal: 2. Zhu Shou of Qin was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Qin dismissed Zhu Shou.

sentences.zh: 魏冉復為丞相，封於穰與陶，謂之穰侯。

translations.literal: Wei Ran again became chancellor, was enfeoffed at Rang and Tao, and was styled the Marquis of Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ran again became chancellor, was enfeoffed at Rang and Tao, and was called the Marquis of Rang.

sentences.zh: 又封公子市於宛，公子悝於鄧。

translations.literal: He also enfeoffed Lord Shi at Wan and Lord Kui at Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed Lord Shi at Wan and Lord Kui at Deng.

sentences.zh: 1魏入河東地四百里、韓入武遂地二百里于秦。

translations.literal: 1. Wei ceded four hundred li of Hedong territory and Han ceded two hundred li of Wusui territory to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Wei ceded four hundred li in Hedong and Han ceded two hundred li at Wusui to Qin.

sentences.zh: 2魏芒卯始以詐見重。

translations.literal: 2. Mang Mao of Wei first came to be valued for his cunning.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Mang Mao of Wei first won favor through deceit.

sentences.zh: 1秦大良造白起、客卿錯伐魏，至軹，取城大小六十一。

translations.literal: 1. Bai Qi, Qin Grand Minister of Construction, and the guest-minister Cuo attacked Wei, reached Zhi, and took sixty-one cities large and small.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Qin Grand Minister Bai Qi and guest-minister Cuo attacked Wei, reached Zhi, and took sixty-one cities large and small.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，秦王稱西帝，遣使立齊王為東帝，欲約與共伐趙。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the king of Qin styled himself Western Emperor and sent envoys to establish the king of Qi as Eastern Emperor, wishing to covenant with him to attack Zhao jointly.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the king of Qin took the title Western Emperor and sent envoys to make the king of Qi Eastern Emperor, proposing a joint attack on Zhao.

sentences.zh: 蘇代自燕來，齊王曰：「秦使魏冉致帝，子以為何如？

translations.literal: Su Dai came from Yan; the king of Qi said: "Qin sent Wei Ran to offer the title of emperor—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Su Dai came from Yan; the king of Qi said: "Qin sent Wei Ran to offer the imperial title—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「願王受之而勿稱也。

translations.literal: " He answered: "I wish Your Majesty to accept it but not proclaim it.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "Accept it, Majesty, but do not proclaim it yourself.

sentences.zh: 秦稱之，天下安之，王乃稱之，無後也。

translations.literal: If Qin proclaims it and the realm is at peace, then Your Majesty may proclaim it—you will not be late.
translations.idiomatic: Let Qin proclaim it first; if the realm accepts that, then proclaim it yourself—you will not be behindhand.

sentences.zh: 秦稱之，天下惡之，王因勿稱，以收天下，此大資也。

translations.literal: Qin adopts the title, the realm hates it—Your Majesty therefore should not adopt it, to win the realm; this is a great asset.
translations.idiomatic: Qin has taken the title and the world hates it—Your Majesty should therefore not take it, to win all under Heaven; this is a great advantage.

sentences.zh: 且伐趙孰與伐桀宋利？

translations.literal: Moreover, is attacking Zhao or attacking tyrannical Song more profitable?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, which is more profitable—attacking Zhao or attacking tyrannical Song?

sentences.zh: 今王不如釋帝以收天下之望，發兵以伐桀宋，宋舉則楚、趙、梁、衛皆懼矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty would do better to relinquish the title of emperor to win the realm’s hopes, raise troops to attack tyrannical Song—when Song is taken, Chu, Zhao, Liang, and Wei will all be afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty would do better to yield the imperial title and win the world’s goodwill, march against tyrannical Song—when Song falls, Chu, Zhao, Liang, and Wei will all fear you.

sentences.zh: 是我以名尊秦而令天下憎之，所謂以卑為尊也。

translations.literal: This would be for us to honor Qin in name and make the realm hate it—what is called making the base the honored.
translations.idiomatic: That would honor Qin in name and make the world hate us—what they call treating the lowly as supreme.

sentences.zh: 」齊王從之，稱帝二日而復歸之。

translations.literal: ” The king of Qi followed this; he took the title of emperor for two days and then returned it.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king of Qi agreed; he styled himself emperor for two days, then gave the title back.

sentences.zh: 十二月，呂禮自齊入秦，秦王亦去帝復稱王。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Lü Li came from Qi into Qin; the king of Qin also abandoned the title of emperor and again styled himself king.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Lü Li went from Qi to Qin; the king of Qin likewise dropped the imperial title and again styled himself king.

sentences.zh: 2秦攻趙，拔杜陽。

translations.literal: 2. Qin attacked Zhao and took Duyang.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Qin attacked Zhao and seized Duyang.

sentences.zh: 1秦司馬錯擊魏河內。

translations.literal: 1. Sima Cuo of Qin struck Wei’s Henei.
translations.idiomatic: 1. Sima Cuo of Qin attacked Henei in Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏獻安邑以和，秦出其人歸之魏。

translations.literal: Wei presented Anyi to make peace; Qin released the people there and returned them to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ceded Anyi to make peace; Qin released the inhabitants and sent them back to Wei.

sentences.zh: 2秦敗韓師于夏山。

translations.literal: 2. Qin defeated Han’s army at Mount Xia.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Qin defeated the Han army at Mount Xia.

sentences.zh: 3宋有雀生𪄟於城之陬。

translations.literal: 3. In Song a sparrow gave birth to a hawk at a corner of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: 3. In Song a sparrow hatched a hawk at a corner of the city wall.

sentences.zh: 史占之，曰：「吉。

translations.literal: The historiographer divined and said: “Auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer divined and said: “Auspicious.

sentences.zh: 小而生巨，必霸天下。

translations.literal: The small producing the great—you will surely dominate the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The small producing the great—you will surely dominate the realm.

sentences.zh: 」宋康王喜，起兵滅滕；

translations.literal: ” King Kang of Song rejoiced, raised troops and destroyed Teng;
translations.idiomatic: ” King Kang of Song rejoiced, raised troops, and destroyed Teng;

sentences.zh: 伐薛；

translations.literal: attacked Xue;
translations.idiomatic: attacked Xue;

sentences.zh: 東敗齊，取五城；

translations.literal: in the east defeated Qi and took five cities;
translations.idiomatic: in the east defeated Qi and took five cities;

sentences.zh: 南敗楚，取地三百里，西敗魏軍。

translations.literal: in the south defeated Chu and took three hundred li of territory; in the west defeated Wei’s army.
translations.idiomatic: in the south defeated Chu and took three hundred li of territory; in the west defeated Wei’s army.

sentences.zh: 與齊、魏為敵國，乃愈自信其霸。

translations.literal: He made enemies of Qi and Wei, and grew ever more confident in his hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: He made enemies of Qi and Wei and grew ever more confident in his hegemony.

sentences.zh: 欲霸之亟成，故射天笞地，斬社稷而焚滅之，以示威服鬼神。

translations.literal: Wishing his hegemony to be quickly achieved, he shot at Heaven and whipped the earth, cut down the altars of soil and grain and burned them, to show his power and subdue spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Eager to complete his hegemony at once, he shot at Heaven, whipped the earth, destroyed the altars of soil and grain and burned them, to awe spirits and demons.

sentences.zh: 為長夜之飲於室中，室中人呼萬歲，則堂上之人應之，堂下之人又應之，門外之人又應之，以至於國中，無敢不呼萬歲者。

translations.literal: He held night-long revels in his chamber; when those in the chamber cried “Long live the king!,” those in the hall answered; those below the hall answered again; those outside the gate answered again—extending through the state, none dared not cry “Long live the king!”
translations.idiomatic: He held all-night revels indoors; when those in the chamber shouted “Long live the king!,” those in the hall echoed; those below echoed again; those outside echoed again—through the whole state none dared not shout “Long live the king!”

sentences.zh: 天下之人謂之「桀宋」。

translations.literal: Men throughout the realm called him “tyrannical Song.”
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven called him “tyrannical Song.”

sentences.zh: 齊湣王起兵伐之，民散，城不守。

translations.literal: King Min of Qi raised troops to attack him; the people scattered and the cities could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: King Min of Qi marched against him; the people scattered and the cities could not be defended.

sentences.zh: 宋王奔魏，死於溫。

translations.literal: The king of Song fled to Wei and died at Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Song fled to Wei and died at Wen.

sentences.zh: 1秦王會楚王於宛，會趙王於中陽。

translations.literal: 1. The king of Qin met the king of Chu at Wan and met the king of Zhao at Zhongyang.
translations.idiomatic: 1. The king of Qin met the king of Chu at Wan and the king of Zhao at Zhongyang.

sentences.zh: 2秦蒙武擊齊，拔九城。

translations.literal: 2. Meng Wu of Qin attacked Qi and took nine cities.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Meng Wu of Qin attacked Qi and seized nine cities.

sentences.zh: 3齊湣王既滅宋而驕，乃南侵楚，西侵三晉，欲并二周，為天子。

translations.literal: 3. King Min of Qi, having destroyed Song, grew arrogant; he then invaded Chu in the south, the Three Jins in the west, wished to annex the two Zhou domains, and become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 3. King Min of Qi, after destroying Song, grew arrogant; he invaded Chu in the south and the Three Jins in the west, sought to swallow the two Zhou capitals, and make himself Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 狐咺正議，斫之檀衢，陳舉直言，殺之東閭。

translations.literal: Hu Hu offered straight counsel and was hewn apart at Tan Qu; Chen Ju spoke bluntly and was killed at Dong Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hu spoke forthrightly and was hacked to death at Tan Qu; Chen Ju spoke plainly and was executed at Dong Lü.

sentences.zh: 燕昭王日夜撫循其人，益為富實，乃與樂毅謀伐齊。

translations.literal: King Zhao of Yan day and night comforted and guided his people, made them ever richer and stronger, and then joined Yue Yi in plotting to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Yan day and night cared for his people, made the state ever richer and stronger, and plotted with Yue Yi to attack Qi.

sentences.zh: 樂毅曰：「齊，霸國之餘業也。

translations.literal: Yue Yi said: “Qi retains the legacy of a hegemon state.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi said: “Qi retains the legacy of a hegemon state.

sentences.zh: 地大人眾，未易獨攻也。

translations.literal: Its territory is large and its population many—not easy to attack alone.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory is large and its population many—not easy to attack alone.

sentences.zh: 王必欲伐之。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must attack it,
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty is determined to attack it,

sentences.zh: 莫如約趙及楚、魏。

translations.literal: nothing is better than allying with Zhao as well as Chu and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: nothing is better than allying with Zhao, Chu, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 」於是使樂毅約趙，別使使者連楚、魏，且令趙啖秦以伐齊之利。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon sent Yue Yi to treat with Zhao, separately sent envoys to link Chu and Wei, and moreover had Zhao entice Qin with the profit of attacking Qi.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent Yue Yi to treat with Zhao, dispatched separate envoys to Chu and Wei, and had Zhao entice Qin with the gains of a campaign against Qi.

sentences.zh: 諸侯害齊王之驕暴，皆爭合謀與燕伐齊。

translations.literal: The feudal lords resented King Min of Qi’s arrogance and violence; all vied to join in plotting with Yan to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords resented King Min’s arrogance and cruelty; all rushed to ally with Yan against Qi.

sentences.zh: 1燕王悉起兵，以樂毅為上將軍。

translations.literal: 1. The king of Yan mustered all troops and made Yue Yi supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: 1. The king of Yan mobilized his entire army and made Yue Yi supreme general.

sentences.zh: 秦尉斯離帥師與三晉之師會之。

translations.literal: Wei Sili, Qin’s commandant, led his army and joined the armies of the Three Jins.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sili, Qin’s commandant, led his army to join the forces of the Three Jins.

sentences.zh: 趙王以相國印授樂毅，樂毅並將秦、魏、韓、趙之兵以伐齊。

translations.literal: The king of Zhao gave Yue Yi the seal of chancellor; Yue Yi jointly commanded the armies of Qin, Wei, Han, and Zhao to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhao gave Yue Yi the chancellor’s seal; Yue Yi commanded the armies of Qin, Wei, Han, and Zhao against Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊湣王悉國中之眾以拒之，戰於濟西，齊師大敗。

translations.literal: King Min of Qi mustered all within the state to resist; they fought west of the Ji River and Qi’s army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: King Min mobilized every man in Qi to resist; west of the Ji River the Qi army was routed.

sentences.zh: 樂毅還秦、韓之師，分魏師以略宋地，部趙師以收河間，身率燕師，長驅逐北。

translations.literal: Yue Yi sent back the armies of Qin and Han, divided the Wei army to seize Song territory, assigned the Zhao army to recover Hejian, and himself led the Yan army in a long drive northward in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi sent the Qin and Han armies home, detached the Wei force to seize Song lands, assigned the Zhao force to recover Hejian, and himself led the Yan army in a long pursuit north.

sentences.zh: 劇辛曰：「齊大而燕小，賴諸侯之助以破其軍，宜及時攻取其邊城以自益，此長久之利也。

translations.literal: Ju Xin said: “Qi is great and Yan small; relying on the feudal lords’ help you broke their army—you should promptly attack and take border cities to enrich yourselves; this is a lasting profit.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Xin said: “Qi is great and Yan small; with the lords’ help you broke their army—you should seize border cities at once to strengthen yourselves; that is lasting gain.

sentences.zh: 今過而不攻，以深入為名，無損於齊，無益於燕，而結深怨，後必悔之。

translations.literal: Now you pass cities without attacking, taking deep penetration as your reputation—no harm to Qi, no benefit to Yan, yet you forge deep enmity; later you will surely regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Now you march past cities without taking them, making a name for deep penetration—no harm to Qi, no gain for Yan, yet you forge deep hatred; you will regret it later.

sentences.zh: 」樂毅曰：「齊王伐功矜能，謀不逮下，廢黜賢良，信任諂諛，政令戾虐，百姓怨懟。

translations.literal: ” Yue Yi said: “The king of Qi boasts of achievements and flatters his abilities; his plans do not reach down to his subordinates; he deposes the worthy, trusts flatterers; his government orders are cruel and perverse, and the people resent and murmur.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yue Yi said: “The king of Qi boasts of his feats and flatters his own talent; his counsel does not reach his subordinates; he dismisses the worthy and trusts sycophants; his edicts are cruel and perverse, and the people murmur in resentment.

sentences.zh: 今軍皆破亡，若因而乘之，其民必叛，禍亂內作，則齊可圖也。

translations.literal: Now their army is all broken and destroyed—if we press the opportunity, its people are sure to rebel; disaster and turmoil arise within, and Qi can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Now their army is destroyed—press the moment and the people will rebel; turmoil within will make Qi ripe for the taking.

sentences.zh: 若不遂乘之，待彼悔前之非，改過恤下而撫其民，則難慮也。

translations.literal: If we do not press the advantage now, and wait until he repents his former faults, reforms and cares for his subordinates and comforts his people, then it will be hard to plan against.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not press now, and wait until he repents his faults, reforms, cares for his subordinates, and comforts his people, he will be hard to overcome.

sentences.zh: 」遂進軍深入。

translations.literal: ” He then advanced the army in depth.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then drove the army deep into Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊人果大亂失度，湣王出走。

translations.literal: The people of Qi indeed fell into great disorder and lost their bearings; King Min fled.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi fell into chaos; King Min fled.

sentences.zh: 樂毅入臨淄，取寶物、祭器，輸之於燕。

translations.literal: Yue Yi entered Linzi, took treasures and ritual vessels, and sent them to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi entered Linzi, took treasures and ritual vessels, and sent them to Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕王親至濟上勞軍，行賞饗士，封樂毅為昌國君，遂使留徇齊城之未下者。

translations.literal: The king of Yan personally came to the Ji River to comfort the army, bestowed rewards and feasted the soldiers, enfeoffed Yue Yi as lord of Changguo, and then had him remain to reduce Qi’s cities not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yan came in person to the Ji to review the troops, rewarded and feasted the army, enfeoffed Yue Yi as lord of Changguo, and left him to reduce the Qi cities still holding out.

sentences.zh: 齊王出亡之衛，衛君辟宮舍之，稱臣而共具。

translations.literal: The king of Qi went out in exile to Wei; the lord of Wei vacated a palace to lodge him, styled himself minister, and shared provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi fled to the state of Wei; its ruler vacated a palace for him, styled himself a minister, and shared his table.

sentences.zh: 齊王不遜，衛人侵之。

translations.literal: The king of Qi was insolent; the people of Wei attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi was insolent; the men of Wei attacked him.

sentences.zh: 齊王去奔鄒、魯，有驕色，鄒、魯弗內，遂走莒。

translations.literal: The king of Qi left and fled to Zou and Lu; he had a proud demeanor, and Zou and Lu would not admit him; he then fled to Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi left for Zou and Lu with a proud bearing; neither state would admit him, and he fled to Ju.

sentences.zh: 楚使淖齒將兵救齊，因為齊相。

translations.literal: Chu sent Nao Chi to lead troops to rescue Qi and thereby became Qi’s chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Chu sent Nao Chi with an army to rescue Qi and made him Qi’s chancellor.

sentences.zh: 淖齒欲與燕分齊地，乃執湣王而數之曰：「千乘、博昌之間，方數百里，雨血沾衣，王知之乎？

translations.literal: Nao Chi wished to divide Qi’s territory with Yan; he thereupon seized King Min and reckoned his crimes, saying: “Between the domain of a thousand chariots and Bochang, for several hundred li, rain of blood soaked garments—did Your Majesty know this?
translations.idiomatic: Nao Chi wished to divide Qi’s lands with Yan; he seized King Min and recounted his crimes: “Between your thousand-chariot realm and Bochang, over hundreds of li, blood rained and soaked garments—did Your Majesty know?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「知之。

translations.literal: ” He said: “I knew it.
translations.idiomatic: ” He said: “I knew it.

sentences.zh: 」「贏、博之間，地坼及泉，王知之乎？

translations.literal: ”“Between Ying and Bo, the earth split to the springs—did Your Majesty know this?
translations.idiomatic: ”“Between Ying and Bo the earth split to the springs—did Your Majesty know?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「知之。

translations.literal: ” He said: “I knew it.
translations.idiomatic: ” He said: “I knew it.

sentences.zh: 」「有人當闕而哭者，求之不得，去則聞其聲，王知之乎？

translations.literal: ”“There was one who stood at the gate and wept; sought, he could not be found; when one left, his voice was heard—did Your Majesty know this?
translations.idiomatic: ”“Someone wept at the gate; sought, he could not be found; when you left, you still heard his voice—did Your Majesty know?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「知之。

translations.literal: ” He said: “I knew it.
translations.idiomatic: ” He said: “I knew it.

sentences.zh: 」淖齒曰：「天雨血沾衣者，天以告也；

translations.literal: ” Nao Chi said: “When Heaven rains blood that soaks garments, Heaven is informing you;
translations.idiomatic: ” Nao Chi said: “When Heaven rains blood that soaks garments, Heaven is warning you;

sentences.zh: 地坼及泉者，地以告也；

translations.literal: when the earth splits to the springs, the earth is informing you;
translations.idiomatic: when the earth splits to the springs, Earth is warning you;

sentences.zh: 有人當闕而哭者，人以告也。

translations.literal: when one stands at the gate and weeps, men are informing you.
translations.idiomatic: when someone weeps at the gate, men are warning you.

sentences.zh: 天、地、人皆告矣，而王不知誡焉，何得無誅！

translations.literal: Heaven, earth, and men have all informed you, yet Your Majesty did not heed and warn yourself—how can you escape execution!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, and men have all warned you, yet Your Majesty would not repent—how can you escape punishment!

sentences.zh: 」遂弒王於鼓里。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon assassinated the king at Guli.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then assassinated the king at Guli.

sentences.zh: 荀子論之曰：國者，天下之利勢也。

translations.literal: Xunzi discussed it, saying: The state is the profit and power of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi commented: The state is the profit and power of the realm.

sentences.zh: 得道以持之，則大安也，大榮也，積美之源也。

translations.literal: Hold it by the Way and there is great security, great glory—the source of accumulated excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Held by the Way, it brings great security and great glory—the source of accumulated excellence.

sentences.zh: 不得道以持之，則大危也，大累也，有之不如無之。

translations.literal: Fail to hold it by the Way and there is great peril, great burden—having it is not as good as not having it.
translations.idiomatic: Held without the Way, it brings great peril and great burden—better not to have it at all.

sentences.zh: 及其綦也，索為匹夫，不可得也。

translations.literal: When it reaches the extreme, to seek to be a common man is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: At the extreme, one cannot even become a common man.

sentences.zh: 齊湣、宋獻是也。

translations.literal: King Min of Qi and King Xian of Song were such cases.
translations.idiomatic: King Min of Qi and King Xian of Song are examples.

sentences.zh: 故用國者義立而王，信立而霸，權謀立而亡。

translations.literal: Thus one who uses the state: when righteousness is established, he becomes king; when trust is established, he becomes hegemon; when schemes of power are established, he perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for one who wields a state: establish righteousness and you may become king; establish trust and you may become hegemon; establish schemes of power and you perish.

sentences.zh: 挈國以呼禮義也，而無以害之。

translations.literal: Take up the state to call forth ritual and righteousness, and nothing can harm it.
translations.idiomatic: Take up the state to proclaim ritual and righteousness, and nothing can harm it.

sentences.zh: 行一不義，殺一無罪，而得天下，仁者不為也。

translations.literal: To perform one unrighteous act, kill one innocent man, and gain the realm—the benevolent do not do this.
translations.idiomatic: To commit one injustice, kill one innocent man, and win the realm—the benevolent will not do it.

sentences.zh: 擽然扶持心國，且若是其固也。

translations.literal: With ardent effort uphold the state in one’s heart, and it is thus firm.
translations.idiomatic: Uphold the state wholeheartedly with ardent effort, and it is firm indeed.

sentences.zh: 之所與為之者之人，則舉義士也；

translations.literal: Those with whom one acts are wholly men of righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Those with whom one associates are wholly men of righteousness;

sentences.zh: 之所以為布陳於國家刑法者，則舉義法也；

translations.literal: what one deploys as law and punishment throughout the state is wholly righteous law;
translations.idiomatic: the laws and punishments one deploys throughout the state are wholly righteous law;

sentences.zh: 主之所極然，帥群臣而首向之者，則舉義志也。

translations.literal: what the ruler aims at utterly, leading his ministers and turning to face first, is wholly righteous purpose.
translations.idiomatic: what the ruler aims at utterly, leading his ministers to face first, is wholly righteous purpose.

sentences.zh: 定而國定，國定而天下定。

translations.literal: When the foundation is established, the state is established; when the state is established, the realm is established.
translations.idiomatic: When the foundation is firm, the state is firm; when the state is firm, the realm is firm.

sentences.zh: 故曰：以國濟義，一日而白，湯、武是也。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: use the state to complete righteousness, and in one day you are made clear—Tang and Wu were such.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said: use the state to fulfill righteousness, and in a day you shine forth—Tang and Wu did so.

sentences.zh: 是所謂義立而王也。

translations.literal: This is what is called establishing righteousness and becoming king.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called establishing righteousness and becoming king.

sentences.zh: 德雖未至也，義雖未濟也，然而天下之理略奏矣，刑賞已諾信乎天下矣，臣下曉然皆知其可要也。

translations.literal: Though virtue has not yet arrived and righteousness has not yet been completed, yet the principles of the realm are roughly achieved; punishments and rewards have already been pledged and trusted by the realm; ministers and subordinates clearly all know what is essential.
translations.idiomatic: Though virtue is not yet complete and righteousness not yet fulfilled, the principles of the realm are roughly in place; punishments and rewards are pledged and trusted throughout the realm; ministers clearly know what matters.

sentences.zh: 政令已陳，雖睹利敗，不欺其民；

translations.literal: Government orders have been proclaimed; though one sees profit fail, one does not deceive the people;
translations.idiomatic: Edicts have been proclaimed; though profit fails, one does not deceive the people;

sentences.zh: 約結已定，雖睹利敗，不欺其與。

translations.literal: Covenant bonds are already fixed; though one sees profit fail, one does not cheat one's allies.
translations.idiomatic: Once covenants are set, even when profit fails, one does not cheat one's allies.

sentences.zh: 如是，則兵勁城固，敵國畏之；

translations.literal: If so, then troops are strong and walls firm, and enemy states fear one;
translations.idiomatic: Then arms are keen and walls secure, and enemy states fear you;

sentences.zh: 國一綦明，與國信之。

translations.literal: the state is unified and utmost clarity prevails, and allied states trust it.
translations.idiomatic: the state is united and utterly clear, and allied states trust it.

sentences.zh: 雖在僻陋之國，威動天下，五伯是也。

translations.literal: Though in a remote and mean state, its awesomeness shakes all under Heaven—the Five Hegemons were such.
translations.idiomatic: Though seated in a remote and poor state, their might shook the realm—the Five Hegemons were such.

sentences.zh: 是所謂信立而而霸也。

translations.literal: This is what is called establishing trust and becoming hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called establishing trust and achieving hegemony.

sentences.zh: 挈國以呼功利，不務張其義，齊其信，唯利之求；

translations.literal: To lead the state crying out for profit and utility, not striving to spread righteousness, align trustworthiness, seeking only profit;
translations.idiomatic: To lead the state in shouting for profit, not striving to spread righteousness or align trust, seeking only gain;

sentences.zh: 內則不憚詐其民而求小利焉，外則不憚詐其與而求大利焉。

translations.literal: inwardly not shrinking from deceiving one's people to seek small profit, outwardly not shrinking from deceiving one's allies to seek great profit.
translations.idiomatic: inwardly not hesitating to cheat one's people for small gain, outwardly not hesitating to cheat one's allies for great gain.

sentences.zh: 內不修正其所以有，然常欲人之有，如是，則臣下百姓莫不以詐心待其上矣。

translations.literal: Inwardly not correcting what one possesses, yet constantly desiring what others possess—if so, then ministers and common folk all treat their superiors with deceit in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly not setting right what one already has, yet always coveting what others hold—then ministers and people alike meet their superiors with deceit in heart.

sentences.zh: 上詐其下，下詐其上，則是上下析也。

translations.literal: Superiors deceive subordinates, subordinates deceive superiors—then above and below are sundered.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors cheat subordinates, subordinates cheat superiors—then above and below are split apart.

sentences.zh: 如是，則敵國輕之，與國疑之，權謀日行而國不免危削，綦之而亡，齊湣、薛公是也。

translations.literal: If so, enemy states despise one, allied states doubt one, plots and schemes practiced daily yet the state cannot escape peril and diminution, at the utmost it perishes—King Min of Qi and Lord Xue were such.
translations.idiomatic: Then enemy states despise you, allies doubt you, stratagems multiply daily yet the state cannot escape danger and shrinkage, and at the extreme it perishes—King Min of Qi and Lord Xue were such.

sentences.zh: 故用強齊，非以修禮義也，非以本政教也，非以一天下也，綿綿常以結引馳外為務。

translations.literal: Thus employing mighty Qi was not to cultivate rites and righteousness, not to root government and teaching, not to unify all under Heaven; constantly and ceaselessly making bonding and drawing abroad the task of galloping outward.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the use of mighty Qi was not to cultivate rites and righteousness, not to ground government and teaching, not to unify the realm—it constantly made alliance-building and outward campaigning its business.

sentences.zh: 故強，南足以破楚，西足以詘秦，北足以敗燕，中足以舉宋。

translations.literal: Hence when strong: south sufficient to break Chu, west sufficient to humble Qin, north sufficient to defeat Yan, central sufficient to overthrow Song.
translations.idiomatic: When it was strong, south it could break Chu, west humble Qin, north defeat Yan, and in the center overthrow Song.

sentences.zh: 及以燕、趙起而攻之，若振槁然，而身死國亡，為天下大戮，後世言惡則必稽焉。

translations.literal: When Yan and Zhao rose to attack it, it was like shaking dry stalks; yet body perished and state was lost, becoming a great disgrace under Heaven—later ages speaking of evil must cite it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan and Zhao rose against it, Qi fell like shaken dry stalks—yet its ruler died and its state perished, a great shame under Heaven; later ages naming evil must cite it.

sentences.zh: 是無他故焉，唯其不由禮義而由權謀也。

translations.literal: This has no other reason—only that it did not proceed by rites and righteousness but by plots and schemes.
translations.idiomatic: There is no other cause—only that it followed not rites and righteousness but plots and schemes.

sentences.zh: 三者，明主之所謹擇也，仁人之所務白也。

translations.literal: These three paths—a wise lord carefully chooses among them; a humane person makes it his business to clarify them.
translations.idiomatic: These three courses a wise ruler carefully chooses; a humane man labors to make them clear.

sentences.zh: 善擇者制人，不善擇者人制之。

translations.literal: Those who choose well control others; those who choose poorly are controlled by others.
translations.idiomatic: Those who choose well control others; those who choose poorly are controlled by others.

translations.literal: Yan troops pressed the victory in long pursuit; Qi cities all fled before the wind in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Yan armies pressed the victory in long pursuit; Qi cities everywhere fled at the rumor of their coming.

sentences.zh: 樂毅修整燕軍，禁止侵掠，求齊之逸民，顯而禮之。

translations.literal: Yue Yi put the Yan army in order, forbade pillage, sought Qi’s scattered people, and honored and treated them with rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi disciplined the Yan army, forbade looting, sought out Qi’s displaced people, and honored them with ceremony.

translations.literal: He then sent the left army across Jiaodong and Donglai;
translations.idiomatic: He sent the left army across Jiaodong and Donglai;

sentences.zh: 前軍循太山以東至海，略琅邪；

translations.literal: the vanguard followed Mount Tai east to the sea and overran Langye;
translations.idiomatic: the vanguard followed Mount Tai east to the sea and seized Langye;

sentences.zh: 右軍循河、濟，屯阿、鄄以連魏師；

translations.literal: the right army followed the Yellow River and Ji, encamped at A and Juancheng to link with Wei’s troops;
translations.idiomatic: the right army followed the Yellow River and Ji, encamped at A and Juancheng to join Wei’s army;

sentences.zh: 後軍旁北海以撫千乘；

translations.literal: the rear army skirted the northern sea to pacify Qiancheng;
translations.idiomatic: the rear army skirted the northern sea to secure Qiancheng;

sentences.zh: 中軍據臨淄而鎮齊都。

translations.literal: the center army held Linzi and stabilized the Qi capital.
translations.idiomatic: the center army held Linzi and secured the Qi capital.

sentences.zh: 祀桓公、管仲於郊，表賢者之閭，封王蠋之墓。

translations.literal: He sacrificed to Duke Huan and Guan Zhong in the suburbs, marked the lanes of worthy men, and enfeoffed Wang Zhu’s tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed to Duke Huan and Guan Zhong in the suburbs, marked the neighborhoods of worthy men, and enfeoffed Wang Zhu’s tomb.

sentences.zh: 齊人食邑於燕者二十餘君，有爵位於薊者百有餘人。

translations.literal: Men of Qi receiving fiefs in Yan numbered more than twenty lords; those holding ranks in Ji numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty Qi men held fiefs in Yan; more than a hundred held titles in Ji.

sentences.zh: 六月之間，下齊七十餘城，皆為郡縣。

translations.literal: Within six months he reduced more than seventy cities of Qi, all made into commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Within six months he took more than seventy Qi cities, all made into commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 3秦王、魏王、韓王會于京師。

translations.literal: 3 The king of Qin, the king of Wei, and the king of Han met at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 3 The kings of Qin, Wei, and Han met at the capital.

sentences.zh: 1秦、趙會于穰。

translations.literal: 1 Qin and Zhao met at Rang.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Qin and Zhao met at Rang.

sentences.zh: 秦拔魏安城，兵至大梁而還。

translations.literal: Qin took Ancheng of Wei; its troops reached Daliang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qin took Wei’s Ancheng, marched to Daliang, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 2齊淖齒之亂，湣王子法章變名姓為莒太史敫家傭。

translations.literal: 2 In the turmoil of Nao Chi in Qi, Min’s son Fajiu changed his name and surname and became a hired man in the household of the Grand Historian of Ju, Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: 2 In the turmoil of Nao Chi in Qi, King Min’s son Fajiu changed his name and worked as a hired hand in the household of Ju’s Grand Historian, Jiao.

sentences.zh: 太史敫女奇法章狀貌，以為非常人，憐而常竊衣食之，因與私通。

translations.literal: Jiao’s daughter marveled at Fajiu’s appearance, thought him no ordinary man, pitied him and often secretly gave him food and clothing, and thereby had relations with him in private.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao’s daughter was struck by Fajiu’s looks, judged him no ordinary man, pitied him and often secretly fed and clothed him, and came to know him intimately.

sentences.zh: 王孫賈從湣王，失王之處，其母曰：「汝朝出而晚來，則吾倚門而望；

translations.literal: Wangsun Jia had followed King Min and lost track of the king’s whereabouts. His mother said: “When you went out in the morning and came back late, I leaned on the door and looked;
translations.idiomatic: Wangsun Jia had followed King Min and lost track of him. His mother said: “When you went out in the morning and came back late, I leaned on the door and watched;

sentences.zh: 汝暮出而不還，則吾倚閭而望。

translations.literal: when you went out at dusk and did not return, I leaned on the lane-end and looked.
translations.idiomatic: when you went out at dusk and did not return, I leaned on the lane-end and watched.

sentences.zh: 汝今事王，王走，汝不知其處，汝尚何歸焉！

translations.literal: Now you serve the king; the king has fled and you do not know where he is—where can you still return!
translations.idiomatic: Now you serve the king; the king has fled and you do not know where—where can you still return!”

sentences.zh: 」王孫賈乃入市中呼曰：「淖齒亂齊國，殺湣王。

translations.literal: ” Wangsun Jia then went into the market and cried: “Nao Chi threw Qi into turmoil and killed King Min.
translations.idiomatic: ” Wangsun Jia went into the market and cried: “Nao Chi threw Qi into turmoil and killed King Min.

sentences.zh: 欲與我誅之者袒右！

translations.literal: Who wishes to join me in executing him, bare your right shoulder!
translations.idiomatic: Who will join me in killing him, bare your right shoulder!”

sentences.zh: 」市人從者四百人，與攻淖齒，殺之。

translations.literal: ” Four hundred men of the market followed him; together they attacked Nao Chi and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Four hundred marketmen followed; together they attacked Nao Chi and killed him.

sentences.zh: 於是齊亡臣相與求湣王子，欲立之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qi’s exiled ministers together sought King Min’s son, wishing to install him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qi’s exiled ministers together sought King Min’s son, intending to set him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 法章懼其誅己，久之乃敢自言，遂立以為齊王，保莒城以拒燕，佈告國中曰：「王已立在莒矣！

translations.literal: Fajiu feared they would execute him; only after a long time did he dare reveal himself. They thereupon installed him as king of Qi, held Ju city to resist Yan, and proclaimed throughout the state: “The king has already been installed at Ju!
translations.idiomatic: Fajiu feared they would kill him; only after long delay did he dare reveal himself. They installed him as king of Qi, held Ju to resist Yan, and proclaimed: “The king has been installed at Ju!”

sentences.zh: 3趙王得楚和氏璧，秦昭王欲之，請易以十五城。

translations.literal: 3 The king of Zhao obtained the He Clan jade of Chu; King Zhao of Qin desired it and asked to exchange it for fifteen cities.
translations.idiomatic: 3 The king of Zhao obtained Chu’s He Clan jade; King Zhao of Qin wanted it and offered fifteen cities in exchange.

sentences.zh: 趙王欲勿與，畏秦強，欲與之，恐見欺。

translations.literal: The king of Zhao wished not to give it, yet feared Qin’s strength; wished to give it, yet feared being deceived.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhao wished to refuse, yet feared Qin’s might; wished to yield it, yet feared being cheated.

sentences.zh: 以問藺相如，對曰：「秦以城求璧而王不許，曲在我矣；

translations.literal: He asked Lin Xiangru, who replied: “If Qin asks for the jade with cities and Your Majesty does not agree, the wrong is on our side;
translations.idiomatic: He asked Lin Xiangru, who answered: “If Qin offers cities for the jade and Your Majesty refuses, the fault is ours;

sentences.zh: 我與之璧而秦不與我城，則曲在秦。

translations.literal: if we give the jade and Qin does not give us cities, then the wrong is on Qin’s side.
translations.idiomatic: if we give the jade and Qin withholds the cities, the fault is Qin’s.

sentences.zh: 均之二策，寧許以負秦。

translations.literal: Weighing the two plans, it is better to agree and lay the blame on Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Between the two courses, better agree and put the blame on Qin.

sentences.zh: 臣願奉璧而往；

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to carry the jade and go;
translations.idiomatic: I will carry the jade there;

sentences.zh: 使秦城不入，臣請完璧而歸之。

translations.literal: if Qin’s cities do not come in, your servant begs to return the jade intact.
translations.idiomatic: if the cities are not delivered, I will return the jade intact.”

sentences.zh: 」趙王遣之。

translations.literal: ” The king of Zhao sent him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king of Zhao sent him.

sentences.zh: 相如至秦，秦王無意償趙城。

translations.literal: Xiangru arrived in Qin; the king of Qin had no intention of paying Zhao with cities.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru reached Qin; the king of Qin had no intention of yielding the cities.

sentences.zh: 相如乃以詐紿秦王，復取璧，遣從者懷之，間行歸趙，而以身待命於秦。

translations.literal: Xiangru then used deceit to beguile the king of Qin, took back the jade, sent a follower to carry it concealed, and by secret route returned to Zhao, while he himself awaited punishment in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru then deceived the king of Qin, recovered the jade, sent a follower to carry it home by a secret route, and himself remained in Qin to await punishment.

sentences.zh: 秦王以為賢而弗誅，禮而歸之。

translations.literal: The king of Qin thought him worthy and did not execute him, but treated him with courtesy and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qin judged him worthy and did not punish him, but honored him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 趙王以相如為上大夫。

translations.literal: The king of Zhao made Xiangru Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhao made Xiangru a grand master.

sentences.zh: 4衛嗣君薨，子懷君立。

translations.literal: 4 Lord Successor of Wei died; his son Lord Huai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: 4 Lord Successor of Wei died; his son Lord Huai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嗣君好察微隱，縣令有發褥而席敝者，嗣君聞之，乃賜之席。

translations.literal: Lord Successor loved to scrutinize minute and hidden matters. A district magistrate had worn out his mat by pulling up the bedding; when Lord Successor heard of it, he bestowed a mat upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Successor loved to detect minute secrets. A magistrate had worn through his mat by turning his bedding; when Lord Successor heard, he sent him a new mat.

sentences.zh: 令大驚，以君為神。

translations.literal: The magistrate was greatly alarmed and took his lord for divine.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate was terrified and took his lord for a god.

sentences.zh: 又使人過關市，賂之以金，既而召關市，問有客過與汝金，汝回遣之，關市大恐。

translations.literal: He also sent someone through the market gate, bribing the gate officer with gold; shortly afterward he summoned the gate officer and asked whether a traveler had passed and given him gold, and whether he had sent it back—the gate officer was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a man through the market gate to bribe the gate officer with gold; then he summoned the officer and asked whether a traveler had given him gold and whether he had returned it—the officer was terrified.

sentences.zh: 又愛洩姬，重如耳，而恐其因愛重以壅己也，乃貴薄疑以敵如耳，尊魏妃以偶泄姬，曰：「以是相參也。

translations.literal: He also loved Lady Xie and favored Ru Er, yet feared that through love and favor they might block him; he therefore exalted Bo Yi to match Ru Er and honored the Wei consort to pair with Lady Xie, saying: “Thus they check one another.
translations.idiomatic: He also favored Lady Xie and prized Ru Er, yet feared they might use favor to hem him in; he therefore elevated Bo Yi to rival Ru Er and honored the Wei consort to balance Lady Xie, saying: “Let them check one another.

sentences.zh: 荀子論之曰：成侯、嗣君，聚斂計數之君也，未及取民也。

translations.literal: Xunzi discussed it, saying: Marquis Cheng and Lord Successor were lords who amassed wealth and reckoned accounts—they had not yet reached taking the people in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi remarked: Marquis Cheng and Lord Successor were rulers who hoarded wealth and counted accounts—they had not yet learned to win the people.

sentences.zh: 子產，取民者也，未及為政也。

translations.literal: Zi Chan was one who took the people in hand—he had not yet reached governing.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Chan won the people—he had not yet reached true government.

sentences.zh: 管仲，為政者也，未及修禮也。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong was one who governed—he had not yet reached cultivating rites.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong governed—he had not yet reached cultivating rites.

sentences.zh: 故修禮者王，為政者強，取民者安，聚斂者亡。

translations.literal: Thus those who cultivate rites become kings, those who govern become strong, those who take the people find security, those who amass and squeeze perish.
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who cultivate rites become kings, those who govern grow strong, those who win the people find security, and those who hoard perish.

sentences.zh: 1秦伐趙，拔兩城。

translations.literal: 1 Qin attacked Zhao and took two cities.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Qin attacked Zhao and took two cities.

sentences.zh: 1秦伐趙，拔石城。

translations.literal: 1 Qin attacked Zhao and took Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Qin attacked Zhao and took Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 2秦穰侯復為丞相。

translations.literal: 2 The Marquis of Rang of Qin again became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: 2 Qin’s Marquis of Rang again became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 3楚欲與齊、韓共伐秦，因欲圖周。

translations.literal: 3 Chu wished to join Qi and Han in attacking Qin, and thereby wished to scheme against Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Chu wished to join Qi and Han in attacking Qin, and also meant to scheme against Zhou.

sentences.zh: 王使東周武公謂楚令尹昭子曰：「周不可圖也。

translations.literal: The king sent the Martial Lord of Eastern Zhou to tell Zhao, chief minister of Chu: “Zhou cannot be schemed against.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent the Martial Lord of Eastern Zhou to tell Chu’s chief minister Zhao: “Zhou cannot be taken by plotting.

sentences.zh: 」昭子曰：「乃圖周，則無之；

translations.literal: ” Zhao said: “As for scheming against Zhou, there is none of that;
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhao said: “As for plotting against Zhou, there is none of that;

sentences.zh: 雖然，何不可圖？

translations.literal: even so, why can it not be schemed against?
translations.idiomatic: even so, why can it not be plotted against?”

sentences.zh: 」武公曰：「西周之地，絕長補短，不過百里。

translations.literal: ” The Martial Lord said: “The lands of Western Zhou, joined end to end and patched short with long, do not exceed a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Martial Lord said: “Western Zhou’s territory, end to end, does not exceed a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 名為天下共主，裂其地不足以肥國，得其眾不足以勁兵。

translations.literal: In name it is the common lord of all under Heaven; to carve up its land is insufficient to enrich a state, to gain its people is insufficient to strengthen an army.
translations.idiomatic: In name it is lord of all under Heaven, yet carving its land would not enrich a state, nor would gaining its people strengthen an army.

sentences.zh: 雖然，攻之者名為弒君。

translations.literal: Even so, those who attack it are named regicides.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, whoever attacks it will be called a regicide.

sentences.zh: 然而猶有欲攻之者，見祭器在焉故也。

translations.literal: Yet still there are those who wish to attack it, because they see the sacrificial vessels are there.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some still wish to attack it—because they see the sacrificial vessels are there.

sentences.zh: 夫虎肉臊而兵利身，人猶攻之；

translations.literal: Now tiger flesh is rank and its body bristles with sharp weapons, yet men still attack it;
translations.idiomatic: Tiger flesh is rank and its body bristles with weapons, yet men still attack it;

sentences.zh: 若使澤中之麋蒙虎之皮，人之攻之也必萬倍矣。

translations.literal: If a marsh deer were to wear a tiger's hide, men's attacking it would surely be ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: If a marsh deer wore a tiger's hide, men would attack it ten thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 裂楚之地，足以肥國；

translations.literal: To carve up Chu's lands would suffice to enrich the state;
translations.idiomatic: Splitting Chu's territory would enrich your state;

sentences.zh: 今子欲誅殘天下之共主，居三代之傳器，器南，則兵至矣。

translations.literal: Now you wish to slaughter the world's common lord, occupy the transmitted vessels of the Three Dynasties—set them facing south, and troops will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Now you would slaughter the lord of all under Heaven, seize the regalia of the Three Dynasties, set them facing south—and armies will come.

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Chu's scheme was abandoned and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thereupon Chu's plan was dropped and not carried out.

sentences.zh: 1秦白起敗趙軍，斬首二萬，取代光狼城。

translations.literal: 1 Qin's Bai Qi defeated Zhao's army, beheaded twenty thousand, and took the city of Guanglang.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Qin's Bai Qi defeated the army of Zhao, beheaded twenty thousand, and took Guanglang.

sentences.zh: 又使司馬錯發隴西兵，因蜀攻楚黔中，拔之。

translations.literal: He also had Sima Cuo raise troops from Longxi, and through Shu attacked Chu's Qianzhong and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Sima Cuo raise Longxi troops and, via Shu, attack Chu's Qianzhong and take it.

sentences.zh: 楚獻漢北及上庸地。

translations.literal: Chu offered the lands north of the Han and Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: Chu yielded the territory north of the Han and Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 1秦白起伐楚，取鄢、鄧、西陵。

translations.literal: 1 Qin's Bai Qi attacked Chu and took Yan, Deng, and Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Qin's Bai Qi attacked Chu and took Yan, Deng, and Xiling.

sentences.zh: 2秦王使使者告趙王，願為好會於河外澠池。

translations.literal: 2 The king of Qin sent an envoy to inform the king of Zhao that he wished to meet in friendship at Mianchi beyond the River.
translations.idiomatic: 2 The king of Qin sent an envoy to the king of Zhao, proposing a friendly meeting at Mianchi beyond the River.

sentences.zh: 趙王欲毋行，廉頗、藺相如計曰：「王不行，示趙弱且怯也。

translations.literal: The king of Zhao wished not to go; Lian Po and Lin Xiangru counselled, saying, “If Your Majesty does not go, it shows Zhao weak and cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhao wished not to go. Lian Po and Lin Xiangru advised: “If Your Majesty does not go, it shows Zhao weak and afraid.

sentences.zh: 」趙王遂行，相如從。

translations.literal: ” The king of Zhao then went, and Xiangru accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king of Zhao went, and Xiangru went with him.

sentences.zh: 廉頗送至境，與王訣曰：「王行，度道里會遇之禮畢，還，不過三十日。

translations.literal: Lian Po escorted him to the border and took leave, saying, “When Your Majesty goes, estimating the distance and the rites of meeting, on return it will not exceed thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Po escorted him to the border and bade farewell: “When Your Majesty goes, reckon the road and the courtesies of the meeting—your return should take no more than thirty days.

sentences.zh: 三十日不還，則請立太子，以絕秦望。

translations.literal: If thirty days pass without return, I beg to establish the crown prince, to cut off Qin's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: If you are not back in thirty days, I ask leave to install the crown prince and cut off Qin's hopes.

sentences.zh: 」王許之。

translations.literal: ” The king assented.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king agreed.

sentences.zh: 會于澠池。

translations.literal: They met at Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: They met at Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 〔秦〕王與趙王飲<ref>〔秦〕王與趙王飲據胡注補。

translations.literal: The 〔Qin〕 king and the king of Zhao drank<ref>The 〔Qin〕 king and the king of Zhao drank—supplemented per Hu's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: The 〔Qin〕 king and the king of Zhao drank<ref>The 〔Qin〕 king and the king of Zhao drank—supplemented per Hu's commentary.

sentences.zh: </ref>，酒酣，秦王請趙王鼓瑟，趙王鼓之。

translations.literal: </ref> When the wine was heated, the king of Qin asked the king of Zhao to play the se; the king of Zhao played.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> When the wine was warm, the king of Qin asked the king of Zhao to play the se, and the king of Zhao played.

sentences.zh: 藺相如復請秦王擊缶，秦王不肯。

translations.literal: Lin Xiangru in turn asked the king of Qin to strike the fou; the king of Qin refused.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xiangru in turn asked the king of Qin to strike the fou; the king of Qin refused.

sentences.zh: 相如曰：「五步之內，臣請得以頸血濺大王矣！

translations.literal: Xiangru said, “Within five paces your servant begs leave to splash his neck-blood upon Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru said, “Within five paces I beg leave to splash my blood on Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 」左右欲刃相如，相如張目叱之，左右皆靡。

translations.literal: ” Those at left and right wished to blade Xiangru; Xiangru glared and shouted them down, and all shrank away.
translations.idiomatic: ” Attendants moved to kill Xiangru; he glared and shouted them down, and all shrank back.

sentences.zh: 王不懌，為一擊缶。

translations.literal: The king was displeased but struck the fou once.
translations.idiomatic: The king was displeased but struck the fou once.

sentences.zh: 罷酒，秦終不能有加於趙。

translations.literal: When the drinking ended, Qin in the end could do nothing more against Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended, Qin could do Zhao no further harm.

sentences.zh: 趙人亦盛為之備，秦不敢動。

translations.literal: The men of Zhao had also made full preparations; Qin did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Zhao had also made full preparations, and Qin did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 趙王歸國，以藺相如為上卿，位在廉頗之右。

translations.literal: The king of Zhao returned to his state and made Lin Xiangru senior minister, ranking to Lian Po's right.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhao returned home, made Lin Xiangru senior minister, and ranked him above Lian Po.

sentences.zh: 廉頗曰：「我為趙將，有攻城野戰之功。

translations.literal: Lian Po said, “I am Zhao's general and have merit in storming cities and field battles.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Po said, “I am Zhao's general. I have merit in storming cities and fighting in the field.

sentences.zh: 藺相如素賤人，徒以口舌而位居我上。

translations.literal: Lin Xiangru was always a low fellow who by words alone ranks above me.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xiangru was always a nobody who ranks above me on words alone.

sentences.zh: 吾羞，不忍為之下！

translations.literal: I am ashamed and cannot bear to rank below him!
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed and cannot bear to stand below him!

sentences.zh: 」宣言曰：「我見相如，必辱之！

translations.literal: ” He declared, “When I see Xiangru I will surely humiliate him!
translations.idiomatic: ” He declared, “When I see Xiangru I will humiliate him!

sentences.zh: 」相如聞之，不肯與會；

translations.literal: ” Xiangru heard this and refused to meet him;
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiangru heard and refused to meet him;

sentences.zh: 每朝，常稱病，不欲爭列。

translations.literal: at each court session he often pleaded illness and did not wish to contend for rank.
translations.idiomatic: at court he often pleaded illness and would not vie for precedence.

sentences.zh: 出而望見，輒引車避匿。

translations.literal: When he went out and saw him in the distance, he would turn his carriage aside to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out and saw him afar, he would turn his carriage aside to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 其舍人皆以為恥。

translations.literal: His retainers all regarded this as shameful.
translations.idiomatic: His retainers all thought this shameful.

sentences.zh: 相如曰：「子視廉將軍孰與秦王？

translations.literal: Xiangru said, “In your view, how does General Lian compare to the king of Qin?
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru said, “How does General Lian compare with the king of Qin, in your view?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不若。

translations.literal: ” They said, “Not equal.
translations.idiomatic: ” They said, “He does not.

sentences.zh: 」相如曰：「夫以秦王之威而相如廷叱之，辱其群臣。

translations.literal: ” Xiangru said, “Yet with the king of Qin's majesty, I publicly shouted him down in court and shamed his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiangru said, “Yet with the king of Qin's power I shouted him down in court and shamed his ministers.

sentences.zh: 相如雖駑，獨畏廉將軍哉！

translations.literal: Though I am slow, would I alone fear General Lian!
translations.idiomatic: Slow as I am, would I fear General Lian alone?

sentences.zh: 顧吾念之，強秦〔之〕所以不敢加兵於趙者<ref>強秦〔之〕所以不敢加兵於趙者章校「十二行本『所』上有『之』字；

translations.idiomatic: But consider: the reason mighty Qin 〔之〕 dares not send troops against Zhao<ref>The reason mighty Qin 〔之〕 dares not send troops against Zhao—Zhang's collation: “In the twelve-line edition ‘之’ appears above ‘所’;

translations.literal: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 孔本同。

translations.literal: Kong's edition agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Kong's edition agrees.

translations.idiomatic: ” Shiji “Biographies of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru” has it; supplemented accordingly.
