translations.literal: </ref> is only because the two of us are here.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> is only because the two of us are here.

sentences.zh: 今兩虎共斗，其勢不俱生。

translations.literal: Now if two tigers fight together, the outcome cannot be that both live.
translations.idiomatic: If two tigers fight, both cannot live.

sentences.zh: 吾所以為此者，先國家之急而後私仇也。

translations.literal: The reason I act thus is to put the state's urgency first and private enmity after.
translations.idiomatic: I act thus because the state's need comes first and private grudges after.

sentences.zh: 」廉頗聞之，肉袒負荊至門射罪，遂為刎頸之交。

translations.literal: ” Lian Po heard this, bared his flesh and bore thorns to his door to declare guilt, and they became friends sworn unto death.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lian Po heard, bared his breast and bore thorns to Xiangru's door to apologize, and they became sworn friends unto death.

sentences.zh: 3初，燕人攻安平，臨淄市掾田單在安平，使其宗人皆以鐵籠傅車槥。

translations.literal: 3 Earlier, when Yan men attacked Anping, Tian Dan, a market clerk of Linzi, was at Anping and had his clansmen all fit iron cages over their carriage shafts.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Earlier, when Yan attacked Anping, Tian Dan, a market clerk of Linzi, was there and had his clansmen fit iron cages over their carriage shafts.

sentences.zh: 及城潰，人爭門而出，皆以轊折車敗，為燕所禽；

translations.literal: When the city fell, men scrambled for the gates to flee; all broke their axles and ruined their carts, and were captured by Yan;
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, men fought for the gates; axles snapped and carts broke, and Yan seized them;

sentences.zh: 獨田單宗人以鐵籠得免，遂奔即墨。

translations.literal: only Tian Dan's clansmen, thanks to the iron cages, escaped, and he fled to Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: only Tian Dan's clan, protected by the iron cages, escaped, and he fled to Jimo.

sentences.zh: 是時齊地皆屬燕，獨莒、即墨未下，樂毅及並右軍、前軍以圍莒，左軍、後軍圍即墨。

translations.literal: At that time all Qi lands belonged to Yan; only Ju and Jimo had not fallen. Yue Yi, together with the merged right and van armies, besieged Ju; the left and rear armies besieged Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: By then all Qi belonged to Yan except Ju and Jimo. Yue Yi, with the united right and van armies, besieged Ju; the left and rear armies besieged Jimo.

sentences.zh: 即墨大夫出戰而死。

translations.literal: The grandee of Jimo went out to battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jimo's commander went out to fight and was killed.

sentences.zh: 即墨人曰：「安平之戰，田單宗人以鐵籠得全，是多智習兵。

translations.literal: The people of Jimo said, “At the battle of Anping, Tian Dan's clansmen were preserved by iron cages—he is very clever and skilled in arms.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jimo said, “At Anping, Tian Dan's clan survived by iron cages—he is clever and knows war.

sentences.zh: 」因共立以為將以拒燕。

translations.literal: ” They therefore together installed him as general to resist Yan.
translations.idiomatic: ” They together made him general to resist Yan.

sentences.zh: 樂毅圍二邑，期年不克，及令解圍，各去城九里而為壘，令曰：「城中民出者勿獲，困者賑之，使即舊業，以鎮新民。

translations.literal: Yue Yi besieged the two cities a full year without taking them; eventually he ordered the siege lifted, each army withdrew nine li from the walls and built camps, and decreed, “Citizens who leave the cities—do not seize them; those in hardship—relieve them; let them resume their old occupations, to reassure the new people.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi besieged the two cities a year without success, then lifted the siege, drew nine li from each wall, and built camps. He decreed: “Let those who leave the cities go free; relieve the distressed; let them return to their trades, to calm the new subjects.

sentences.zh: 」三年而猶未下。

translations.literal: ” Three years passed and they still had not fallen.
translations.idiomatic: ” Three years passed and they still had not fallen.

sentences.zh: 或讒之於燕昭王曰：「樂毅智謀過人，伐齊，呼吸之間剋七十餘城。

translations.literal: Someone slandered him to King Zhao of Yan, saying, “Yue Yi's wisdom and schemes surpass other men; attacking Qi, in the space of a breath he took more than seventy cities.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered him to King Zhao of Yan: “Yue Yi's wit outdoes all men. Attacking Qi, he took more than seventy cities in a breath.

sentences.zh: 今不下者兩城耳，非其力不能拔，所以三年不攻者，欲久仗兵威以服齊人，南面而王耳。

translations.literal: Now only two cities remain untaken—not that his strength cannot uproot them; the reason he has not attacked for three years is that he wishes long to wield military prestige to subdue the men of Qi and be king facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Only two cities remain—not that he cannot take them, but he has not attacked for three years because he means to hold his army's prestige until Qi submits, then be king facing south.

sentences.zh: 今齊人已服，所以未發者，以其妻子在燕故也。

translations.literal: Now the men of Qi have submitted; the reason he has not declared himself is that his wife and children are in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi is already won; he has not declared himself only because his wife and children are in Yan.

sentences.zh: 且齊多美女，又將忘其妻子。

translations.literal: Moreover Qi has many beautiful women—he will again forget his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Qi has many fair women—he will forget wife and children again.

sentences.zh: 願王圖之！

translations.literal: May Your Majesty take thought of this!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty consider this!

sentences.zh: 」昭王於是置酒大會，引言者而讓之曰：「先王舉國以禮賢者，非貪土地以遺子孫也。

translations.literal: ” King Zhao thereupon set out wine for a great assembly, brought forward the accuser and reproved him, saying, “The former king devoted the whole state to honor men of worth—not to covet territory to bequeath descendants.
translations.idiomatic: ” King Zhao then held a great feast, brought forward the accuser, and rebuked him: “The former king devoted the whole state to honor the worthy—not to grab land for his heirs.

sentences.zh: 遭所傳德薄，不能堪命，國人不順。

translations.literal: He met with thin virtue in what was handed down and could not bear the mandate; the people of the state were not compliant.
translations.idiomatic: The virtue he handed down was thin; he could not bear the charge, and the people would not obey.

sentences.zh: 齊為無道，乘孤國之亂以害先王。

translations.literal: Qi was without the Way and seized upon our orphaned state's disorder to harm the former king.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was lawless and seized our orphaned state's disorder to harm the former king.

sentences.zh: 寡人統位，痛之入骨，故廣延群臣，外招賓客，以求報仇。

translations.literal: When I inherited the throne the pain went to the marrow; therefore I widely gathered ministers and outwardly recruited guests, seeking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: When I took the throne the pain went to the bone; I gathered ministers far and wide and recruited guests from without, seeking revenge.

sentences.zh: 其有成功者，尚欲與之同共燕國。

translations.literal: Whoever should succeed—I still intend to share Yan with him.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever succeeded, I meant still to share Yan with him.

sentences.zh: 今樂君親為寡人破齊，夷其宗廟，報塞先仇，齊國固樂君所有，非燕之所得也。

translations.literal: Now Lord Yue has personally for me broken Qi, leveled its ancestral temples, and requited the former grievance—Qi in truth belongs to Lord Yue, not to what Yan can claim.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lord Yue has himself broken Qi for me, razed its temples, and settled the old score—Qi rightly belongs to Lord Yue, not to Yan.

sentences.zh: 樂君若能有齊，與燕並為列國，結歡同好，以抗諸侯之難，燕國之福，寡人之願也。

translations.literal: If Lord Yue can hold Qi and stand with Yan as coequal states, joining friendship and good will to withstand the feudal lords' hardships—that is Yan's blessing and my wish.
translations.idiomatic: If Lord Yue can hold Qi and stand with Yan as equal states, joining in friendship to meet the lords' threats—that is Yan's blessing and my wish.

sentences.zh: 汝何敢言若此！

translations.literal: How dare you speak thus!
translations.idiomatic: How dare you speak thus!

sentences.zh: 」乃斬之。

translations.literal: ” He then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 賜樂毅妻以後服，賜其子以公子之服；

translations.literal: He bestowed on Yue Yi's wife the garb of a queen, on his son the garb of a young lord;
translations.idiomatic: He gave Yue Yi's wife a queen's robes and his son a young lord's dress;

sentences.zh: 輅車乘馬，後屬百兩，遣國相奉而致之樂毅，立樂毅為齊王。

translations.literal: a carriage and team, with a hundred coaches following behind; he sent the state chancellor to convey these to Yue Yi and install Yue Yi as king of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: a carriage and horses, a hundred coaches behind; he sent the chancellor to present them to Yue Yi and install him as king of Qi.

sentences.zh: 樂毅惶恐不受，拜書，以死自誓。

translations.literal: Yue Yi in fear and awe did not accept, bowed in written reply, and pledged himself unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi in fear refused, bowed in writing, and pledged his life.

sentences.zh: 由是齊人服其義，諸侯畏其信，莫敢復有謀者。

translations.literal: From this the men of Qi submitted to his righteousness; the feudal lords feared his faith—none dared again plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Then the men of Qi honored his integrity, the lords feared his loyalty, and none dared plot again.

sentences.zh: 頃之，昭王薨，惠王立。

translations.literal: Before long King Zhao died and King Hui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon King Zhao died and King Hui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 惠王自為太子時，嘗不快於樂毅。

translations.literal: King Hui, from the time he was crown prince, had once been displeased with Yue Yi.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince, King Hui had once been displeased with Yue Yi.

sentences.zh: 田單聞之，乃縱反間於燕，宣言曰：「齊王已死，城之不拔者二耳。

translations.literal: Tian Dan heard this and sent counter-intelligence into Yan, proclaiming, “The king of Qi is already dead; only two cities remain untaken.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan heard and sent disinformation into Yan, proclaiming: “The king of Qi is dead; only two cities still hold out.

sentences.zh: 樂毅與燕新王有隙，畏誅而不敢歸，以伐齊為名，實欲連兵南面王齊。

translations.literal: Yue Yi has a rift with Yan's new king; fearing execution he dares not return. Under the name of attacking Qi he truly wishes to link armies and be king of Qi facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi is at odds with Yan's new king; fearing death he dares not return. He attacks Qi in name only, but means to unite his forces and be king of Qi facing south.

sentences.zh: 齊人未附，故且緩攻即墨以待其事。

translations.literal: The men of Qi are not yet attached; therefore he for now slows the attack on Jimo, awaiting the event.
translations.idiomatic: Qi is not yet won, so he delays the assault on Jimo, waiting for the moment.

sentences.zh: 齊人所懼，唯恐他將之來，即墨殘矣。

translations.literal: What the men of Qi fear is only that another general will come—then Jimo will be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: What Qi fears is only that another general will come—then Jimo will be ruined.

sentences.zh: 」燕王固已疑樂毅，得齊反間，乃使騎劫代將而召樂毅。

translations.literal: ” The king of Yan had already doubted Yue Yi; receiving Qi's counter-intelligence, he sent Qi Jie to replace him as general and summoned Yue Yi.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king of Yan had already doubted Yue Yi; getting Qi's disinformation, he sent Qi Jie to replace him and summoned Yue Yi back.

sentences.zh: 樂毅知王不善代之，遂奔趙。

translations.literal: Yue Yi knew the king's displeasure at replacing him and fled to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi knew the king resented the replacement and fled to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 燕將士由是憤惋不和。

translations.literal: Yan's generals and soldiers from this were angry, resentful, and discordant.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's officers and men from this were angry, aggrieved, and divided.

sentences.zh: 田單令城中人，食必祭其先祖於庭，飛鳥皆翔舞而下城中。

translations.literal: Tian Dan ordered the people in the city, whenever they ate, to sacrifice to their ancestors in the courtyard; flying birds all soared and danced down into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan ordered that whenever the people ate, they sacrifice to their ancestors in the courtyard; birds swooped and danced down into the city.

sentences.zh: 燕人怪之，田單因宣言曰：「當有神師下教我。

translations.literal: The men of Yan found it strange; Tian Dan therefore proclaimed, “A divine teacher is about to descend and instruct me.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops marveled; Tian Dan proclaimed: “A divine teacher is about to descend and instruct me.

sentences.zh: 」有一卒曰：「臣可以為師乎？

translations.literal: ” A soldier said, “May your servant be that teacher?
translations.idiomatic: ” A soldier said, “May I be that teacher?

sentences.zh: 」因反走。

translations.literal: ” and turned and ran.
translations.idiomatic: ” and ran off.

sentences.zh: 田單起引還，坐東鄉，師事之。

translations.literal: Tian Dan rose, pulled him back, seated him facing east, and treated him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan rose, brought him back, seated him facing east, and served him as teacher.

sentences.zh: 卒曰：「臣欺君。

translations.literal: The soldier said, “Your servant deceived you.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier said, “I deceived you.

sentences.zh: 」田單曰：「子勿言也。

translations.literal: ” Tian Dan said, “Say no more.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tian Dan said, “Say no more.

sentences.zh: 」因師之，每出約束，必稱神師。

translations.literal: ” He therefore kept him as teacher; whenever he issued orders he surely invoked the divine teacher.
translations.idiomatic: ” He kept him as teacher; whenever he issued orders he invoked the divine teacher.

sentences.zh: 乃宣言曰：「吾唯懼燕軍之劓所得齊卒，置之前行，即墨敗矣！

translations.literal: He then proclaimed, “I only fear that if Yan's army noses the Qi soldiers they have captured and places them in the van, Jimo will be lost!
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed: “I fear only that if Yan's army cuts the noses of captured Qi soldiers and puts them in the van, Jimo is lost!

sentences.zh: 」燕人聞之，如其言。

translations.literal: ” The men of Yan heard it and acted as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Yan troops heard it and did as he said.

sentences.zh: 城中見降者盡劓，皆怒，堅守，唯恐見得。

translations.literal: In the city, seeing that surrendered men all had their noses cut, all were angry and held firm, fearing only being taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the city, seeing captured men with their noses cut off, all were enraged and held firm, fearing only capture.

sentences.zh: 單又縱反間，言：「吾懼燕人掘吾城外塚墓，可為寒心！

translations.literal: Dan again sent counter-intelligence, saying, “I fear the men of Yan will dig up the graves outside our walls—how chilling to the heart!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan again sent disinformation, saying: “I fear Yan will dig up the graves outside our walls—how chilling!

sentences.zh: 」燕軍盡掘塚墓，燒死人。

translations.literal: ” The Yan army dug up all the graves and burned the dead.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Yan army dug up every grave and burned the corpses.

sentences.zh: 齊人從城上望見，皆涕泣，共欲出戰，怒自十倍。

translations.literal: The men of Qi, looking down from the walls, all wept; together they wished to go out and fight, and their rage increased tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Qi on the walls saw it, wept, and together wanted to sally out; their rage redoubled ten times over.

sentences.zh: 田單知士卒之可用，乃身操版、鍤，與士卒分功；

translations.literal: Tian Dan knew the soldiers could be used; he himself took mattock and spade and shared the work with the troops;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan knew his troops were ready; he himself took mattock and spade and shared their labor;

sentences.zh: 妻妾編於行伍之間；

translations.literal: his wife and concubines wove among the ranks;
translations.idiomatic: his wife and concubines wove among the ranks;

sentences.zh: 盡散飲食饗士。

translations.literal: he gave out all food and drink to feast the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: he gave out all food and drink to feast his men.

sentences.zh: 令甲卒皆伏，使老、弱、女子乘城，遣使約降於燕，燕軍皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: He ordered armored soldiers all to lie hidden, had the old, weak, and women man the walls, sent envoys to treat for surrender with Yan, and the Yan army all shouted “Long live!
translations.idiomatic: He hid the armored troops, put the old, weak, and women on the walls, sent envoys to negotiate surrender with Yan, and the Yan army shouted “Long live!

sentences.zh: 田單又收民金得千鎰，令即墨富豪遺燕將，曰：「即降，願無虜掠吾族家。

translations.literal: Tian Dan also collected from the people a thousand yi in gold and had the wealthy of Jimo present it to the Yan general, saying, “When we surrender, we beg that our clans and homes not be plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan also collected a thousand yi of gold from the people and had Jimo's wealthy present it to the Yan general, saying: “When we surrender, do not plunder our families and homes.

sentences.zh: 」燕將大喜，許之。

translations.literal: ” The Yan general was greatly pleased and promised.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Yan general was delighted and agreed.

sentences.zh: 燕軍益懈。

translations.literal: The Yan army grew still more slack.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army grew still more slack.

sentences.zh: 田單乃收城中，得牛千餘，為絳繒衣，畫以五采龍文，束兵刃於其角，而灌脂束葦於其尾，燒其端，鑿城數十穴，夜縱牛，壯士五千〔人〕隨其後<ref>壯士五千〔人〕隨其後據《史記·田單列傳》補。

translations.literal: Tian Dan then gathered in the city more than a thousand oxen, made crimson silk coats for them, painted them with five-colored dragon designs, bound blades to their horns, poured grease and bound reeds to their tails, burned the tips, bored several dozen holes in the wall, and by night released the oxen, with five thousand 〔men〕 of stout warriors following behind<ref>with five thousand 〔men〕 of stout warriors following behind—supplemented per Shiji “Biography of Tian Dan”.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan then gathered more than a thousand oxen in the city, fitted them with crimson silk coats painted with five-colored dragons, bound blades to their horns, greased and bound reeds to their tails, set the tips afire, bored several dozen holes in the wall, and by night released the oxen, with five thousand 〔men〕 of stout warriors behind<ref>“five thousand 〔men〕 of stout warriors behind”—added from Shiji “Biography of Tian Dan”.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 牛尾熱，怒而奔燕軍。

translations.literal: The oxen's tails burned hot; enraged, they charged the Yan army.
translations.idiomatic: Their tails burned hot; enraged, the oxen charged the Yan army.

sentences.zh: 燕軍大驚，視牛皆龍文，所觸盡死傷。

translations.literal: The Yan army was greatly alarmed; seeing the oxen all bore dragon designs, whatever they touched was killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army panicked; the oxen seemed all dragon-marked, and whatever they struck was killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 而城中鼓噪從之，老弱皆擊銅器為聲，聲動天地。

translations.literal: Meanwhile in the city drums and shouts followed them; old and weak all struck bronze vessels for sound—the noise shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the city drummed and shouted in pursuit; young and old beat bronze vessels until the noise shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 燕軍大駭，敗走。

translations.literal: The Yan army was greatly terrified and fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army was terrified and fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 齊人殺騎劫，追亡逐北，所過城邑皆叛燕，復為齊。

translations.literal: The men of Qi killed Qi Jie, pursued the fleeing and routed the northward; every city they passed rebelled against Yan and returned to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Qi killed Qi Jie and pursued the fugitives; every city they passed rebelled against Yan and returned to Qi.

sentences.zh: 田單兵日益多，乘勝，燕日敗亡，走至河上，而齊七十餘城皆復焉。

translations.literal: Tian Dan's troops daily grew more numerous; riding victory, Yan daily was defeated and destroyed, fleeing to the river—and more than seventy cities of Qi were all restored.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan's army grew daily; pressing the victory, Yan fell back day by day to the river, and more than seventy cities of Qi were restored.

sentences.zh: 乃迎襄王於莒。

translations.literal: He thereupon welcomed King Xiang from Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He then welcomed King Xiang from Ju.

sentences.zh: 入臨淄，封田單為安平君。

translations.literal: Entering Linzi, he enfeoffed Tian Dan as Lord of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Linzi, he enfeoffed Tian Dan as Lord of Anping.

sentences.zh: 齊王以太史敫之女為後，生太子建。

translations.literal: The king of Qi took the daughter of Grand Clerk Ji as consort; she bore the crown prince Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi took Grand Clerk Ji's daughter as consort; she bore Crown Prince Jian.

sentences.zh: 太史敫曰：「女不取媒，因自嫁，非吾種也，汙吾世！

translations.literal: Grand Clerk Ji said, “My daughter took no go-between and married of herself—she is not of my kind; she stains my house!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Clerk Ji said: “My daughter took no matchmaker and married on her own—she is not of my blood; she stains my line!

sentences.zh: 」終身不見君王后，君王后亦不以不見故失人子之禮。

translations.literal: ” He never in his life saw the queen; the queen also, on account of not being seen, did not fail in the rites due a parent from a child.
translations.idiomatic: ” He never saw the queen in his life; the queen also, though never received, did not fail in a daughter's duty toward him.

sentences.zh: 趙王封樂毅於觀津，尊寵之，以警動於燕、齊。

translations.literal: The king of Zhao enfeoffed Yue Yi at Guanjin, honored and favored him, to alarm and stir Yan and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhao enfeoffed Yue Yi at Guanjin and honored him lavishly, to warn and stir Yan and Qi.

sentences.zh: 燕惠王乃使人讓樂毅，且謝之曰：「將軍過聽，以與寡人有隙，遂捐燕歸趙。

translations.literal: King Hui of Yan thereupon sent someone to reproach Yue Yi and also apologize, saying, “The general listened too far and, having a rift with me, abandoned Yan and returned to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: King Hui of Yan sent someone to reproach Yue Yi and also to apologize: “General, you listened too readily, took offense at me, abandoned Yan, and went to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 將軍自為計則可矣，而亦何以報先王這所以遇將軍之意乎？

translations.literal: The general may plan for himself—but how will you repay what the former king meant by how he treated the general?
translations.idiomatic: You may look to your own interest—but how will you repay what the former king meant by how he honored you?

sentences.zh: 」樂毅報書曰：「昔伍子胥說聽於闔閭而吳遠跡至郢；

translations.literal: ” Yue Yi replied in writing, saying, “Of old Wu Zixu spoke and was heeded by Helü, and Wu's tracks reached far to Ying;
translations.idiomatic: ” Yue Yi wrote back: “Of old Wu Zixu was heeded by King Helü of Wu, and Wu's armies reached as far as Ying;

sentences.zh: 夫差弗是也，賜之鴟夷而浮之江。

translations.literal: Fuchai did not approve and bestowed on him the owl-skin bag and floated him on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchai would not have it, gave him the leather sack, and set him adrift on the river.

sentences.zh: 吳王不寤先論之可以立功，故沈子胥而不悔；

translations.literal: The king of Wu did not awaken to how the former counsel could establish merit; therefore he drowned Zixu and did not repent;
translations.idiomatic: The king of Wu did not see that the earlier counsel could win merit, so he drowned Zixu unrepentant;

sentences.zh: 子胥不蚤見主之不同量，是以至於入江而不化。

translations.literal: Zixu did not early perceive that his lord's measure differed—thus he came to entering the river and did not transform.
translations.idiomatic: Zixu did not early see that his lord's measure differed—thus he entered the river and was lost.

sentences.zh: 夫免自立功以明先王之跡，臣之上計也。

translations.literal: To escape, establish merit, and clarify the former king's achievement—that is your servant's upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: To escape, win merit, and vindicate the former king's design—that is my best course.

sentences.zh: 離毀辱之誹謗，墮先王之名，臣之所大恐也。

translations.literal: To leave slander of ruin and insult and bring down the former king's name—that is what your servant greatly fears.
translations.idiomatic: To flee slander and disgrace and stain the former king's name—that is what I most fear.

sentences.zh: 臨不測之罪，以幸為利，義之所不敢出也。

translations.literal: Facing unpredictable guilt and taking luck for profit—righteousness dares not offer this.
translations.idiomatic: To face uncertain punishment and take advantage for profit—right conduct forbids it.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之君子，交絕不出惡聲，忠臣去國，不潔其名。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that ancient gentlemen, when breaking off relations, utter no evil sound; loyal ministers who leave a state do not stain their names.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that gentlemen of old, when breaking with someone, spoke no evil; loyal ministers who left a state did not stain their names.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不佞，數奉教於君子矣。

translations.literal: Though your servant is not talented, I have several times received instruction from gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not worthy, I have often been taught by gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 唯君王之留意焉！

translations.literal: May Your Majesty only take thought of this!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty only bear this in mind!

sentences.zh: 」於是燕王復以樂毅子閒為昌國君，而樂毅往來復通燕，卒於趙，號曰望諸君。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the king of Yan again made Yue Yi's son Xian lord of Chang, while Yue Yi went back and forth and again had dealings with Yan; he died in Zhao and was styled Lord Wangzhu.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thereupon the king of Yan again made Yue Yi's son Xian lord of Chang; Yue Yi resumed contact with Yan; he died in Zhao and was styled Lord Wangzhu.

sentences.zh: 田單相齊，過淄水，有老人涉淄而寒，出水不能行。

translations.literal: Tian Dan, as chancellor of Qi, crossed the Zi River; an old man forded the Zi and was cold—coming out of the water he could not walk.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor of Qi, Tian Dan was crossing the Zi when an old man waded the river, took cold, and could not walk after coming out.

sentences.zh: 田單解其裘而衣之。

translations.literal: Tian Dan removed his fur coat and clothed him in it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan took off his fur coat and put it on him.

sentences.zh: 襄王惡之，曰：「田單之施於人，將〔欲〕以取我國乎<ref>將〔欲〕以取我國乎據《史記·田單列傳》補。

translations.literal: King Xiang resented it and said, “Tian Dan's kindness to others—is he 〔wishing〕 to seize my state?<ref>is he 〔wishing〕 to seize my state?—supplemented per Shiji “Biography of Tian Dan”.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiang took offense and said: “Tian Dan's kindness to others—is he 〔trying〕 to take my state?<ref>“〔trying〕 to take my state”—added from Shiji “Biography of Tian Dan”.

sentences.zh: </ref>？

translations.literal: </ref>?
translations.idiomatic: </ref>?

sentences.zh: 不早圖，恐後之變也。

translations.literal: If we do not plan early, I fear trouble later.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act early, I fear trouble later.

sentences.zh: 」左右顧無人，巖下有貫珠者，襄王呼而問之曰：「汝聞吾言乎？

translations.literal: ” He looked to left and right—no one was there; below the cliff was one who strung pearls. King Xiang called and asked him, saying, “Did you hear my words?
translations.idiomatic: ” He looked about—no one was near; below the cliff a pearl-stringer sat. King Xiang called him and asked: “Did you hear what I said?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「聞之。

translations.literal: ” He answered, “I heard.
translations.idiomatic: ” He answered: “I heard.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「汝以為何如？

translations.literal: ” The king said, “What do you think of it?
translations.idiomatic: ” The king said: “What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「王不如因以為己善。

translations.literal: ” He answered, “Your Majesty would do better to turn it to your own credit.
translations.idiomatic: ” He answered: “Your Majesty should turn it to your own credit.

sentences.zh: 王嘉單之善，下令曰：『寡人憂民之飢也，單收而食之；

translations.literal: Your Majesty should praise Dan's goodness and issue an order, saying, ‘I worry that the people hunger—Dan gathers them and feeds them;
translations.idiomatic: Praise Tian Dan's goodness and decree: ‘I worry that the people hunger—Tian Dan gathers them and feeds them;

sentences.zh: 寡人憂民之寒也，單解裘而衣之；

translations.literal: I worry that the people are cold—Dan removes his fur coat and clothes them;
translations.idiomatic: I worry that the people are cold—Tian Dan strips off his fur coat and clothes them;

sentences.zh: 寡人憂勞百姓，而單亦憂〔之〕<ref>而單亦憂〔之〕據《史記·田單列傳》補。

translations.literal: I worry over toiling the hundred surnames, and Dan also worries 〔over it〕<ref>and Dan also worries 〔over it〕—supplemented per Shiji “Biography of Tian Dan”.
translations.idiomatic: I worry over the people's burdens, and Tian Dan worries 〔over them〕 too<ref>“worries 〔over them〕 too”—added from Shiji “Biography of Tian Dan”.

sentences.zh: </ref>，稱寡人之意。

translations.literal: </ref>, echoing my intent.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, echoing my intent.

sentences.zh: 』單有是善而王嘉之，單之善亦王之善也。

translations.literal: ’ When Dan has such goodness and Your Majesty praises it, Dan's goodness is also Your Majesty's goodness.
translations.idiomatic: ’ When Tian Dan does good and Your Majesty praises it, his goodness is Your Majesty's goodness.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「善。

translations.literal: ” The king said, “Good.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king said: “Well said.

sentences.zh: 」乃賜單牛酒。

translations.literal: ” He then bestowed on Dan oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then gave Tian Dan oxen and wine.

sentences.zh: 後數日，貫珠者復見王曰：「王朝日宜召田單而揖之於庭，口勞之。

translations.literal: Several days later the pearl-stringer again saw the king and said, “Your Majesty should daily summon Tian Dan, bow to him in the court, and comfort him with words.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the pearl-stringer saw the king again and said: “Your Majesty should summon Tian Dan each morning, bow to him in court, and speak words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 乃布令求百姓之饑寒者，收穀之。

translations.literal: Then issue a public order seeking among the hundred surnames those who hunger or are cold, and gather grain for them.
translations.idiomatic: Then proclaim that you seek the hungry and cold among the people and will gather grain for them.

sentences.zh: 」乃使人聽於閭里，聞大夫之相與語者曰：「田單之愛人，嗟，乃王之教也！

translations.literal: ” He then had men listen in the lanes and alleys; they heard grandees speaking together, saying, “Tian Dan's love for the people—ah, it is the king's teaching!
translations.idiomatic: ” He had men listen in the lanes; they heard officials saying: “Tian Dan's care for the people—ah, that is the king's teaching!

sentences.zh: 田單任貂勃於王。

translations.literal: Tian Dan entrusted Diao Bo to the king.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan recommended Diao Bo to the king.

sentences.zh: 王有所幸臣九人，欲傷安平君，相與語於王曰：「燕之伐齊之時，楚王使將軍將萬人而佐齊。

translations.literal: The king had nine favored ministers who wished to harm the Lord of Anping; they spoke together to the king, saying, “When Yan attacked Qi, the king of Chu sent a general with ten thousand men to assist Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The king had nine favored ministers who wished to harm Lord Anping; they said to the king: “When Yan attacked Qi, the king of Chu sent a general with ten thousand men to aid Qi.

sentences.zh: 今國已定而社稷已安矣，何不使使者謝於楚王？

translations.literal: Now the state is settled and the altars are secure—why not send an envoy to thank the king of Chu?
translations.idiomatic: Now the state is settled and the altars secure—why not send an envoy to thank the king of Chu?

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「左右孰可？

translations.literal: ” The king said, “Who among those at hand will do?
translations.idiomatic: ” The king said: “Who among my attendants will do?

sentences.zh: 」九人之屬曰：「貂勃可。

translations.literal: ” The nine men's faction said, “Diao Bo will do.
translations.idiomatic: ” The nine said: “Diao Bo will do.

sentences.zh: 」貂勃使楚，楚王受而觴之，數月不反。

translations.literal: ” Diao Bo was sent to Chu; the king of Chu received and feasted him, and for several months he did not return.
translations.idiomatic: ” Diao Bo went to Chu; the king of Chu received and feasted him, and for months he did not return.

sentences.zh: 九人之屬相與語〔於王〕曰<ref>九人之屬相與語〔於王〕曰據《史記·田單列傳》補。

translations.literal: The nine men's faction spoke together 〔to the king〕, saying<ref>spoke together 〔to the king〕, saying—supplemented per Shiji “Biography of Tian Dan”.
translations.idiomatic: The nine spoke together 〔to the king〕, saying<ref>“spoke together 〔to the king〕”—added from Shiji “Biography of Tian Dan”.

sentences.zh: </ref>：「夫一人之身而牽留萬乘者，豈不以據勢也哉！

translations.literal: </ref>: “That one man's person should detain a state of ten thousand chariots—is it not because he holds power!
translations.idiomatic: </ref>: “That one man should hold back a state of ten thousand chariots—is it not because he holds power!

sentences.zh: 且安平君之與王也，君臣無異而上下無別。

translations.literal: Moreover, between the Lord of Anping and Your Majesty there is no difference between minister and lord, nor distinction between above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, between Lord Anping and Your Majesty there is no difference of minister and lord, nor of high and low.

sentences.zh: 且其志欲為不善，內撫百姓，外懷戎翟，禮天下之賢士，其志欲有為〔也〕，願王察之<ref>其志欲有為〔也〕願王察之章校「十二行本『為』下有『也』字，『王』下有『之』字；

translations.literal: Moreover his intent wishes ill; inwardly he comforts the hundred surnames, outwardly he embraces the Rong and Di, treats with rites the worthy men under Heaven—his intent wishes to act 〔也〕; may Your Majesty examine this<ref>his intent wishes to act 〔也〕; may Your Majesty examine this—Zhang's collation: “In the twelve-line edition below ‘act’ is the character ‘也’, and below ‘Majesty’ is the character ‘之’;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he means ill: inwardly he wins the people, outwardly he courts the Rong and Di, honors the worthy under Heaven—he means to act 〔也〕; may Your Majesty look into it<ref>“means to act 〔也〕; may Your Majesty look into it”—Zhang's collation: “In the twelve-line edition ‘也’ follows ‘為’, and ‘之’ follows ‘王’;

sentences.zh: 乙十一行本同；

translations.literal: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 孔本同；

translations.literal: Kong's edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: Kong's edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 退齋校云：『為』下有『也』字。

translations.literal: Tui Zhai's collation says: below ‘act’ is the character ‘也’.
translations.idiomatic: Tui Zhai's collation says: ‘也’ follows ‘為’.

sentences.zh: 」今據補「也」，「之」字不補亦通。

translations.literal: ” Now ‘也’ is supplemented accordingly; not supplementing ‘之’ is also intelligible.
translations.idiomatic: ” ‘也’ is supplemented accordingly; omitting ‘之’ is also intelligible.

sentences.zh: </ref>！

translations.literal: </ref>!
translations.idiomatic: </ref>!

sentences.zh: 」異日，王曰：「召相單而來！

translations.literal: ” Another day the king said, “Summon Chancellor Dan to come!
translations.idiomatic: ” Another day the king said: “Summon Chancellor Tian Dan!

sentences.zh: 」田單免冠、徒跣、肉袒而進，退而請死罪，五日而王曰：「子無罪於寡人。

translations.literal: ” Tian Dan removed cap and shoes, bared his flesh, and advanced; withdrawing he begged the death penalty. Five days later the king said, “You have no guilt toward me.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tian Dan came bareheaded, barefoot, and bare-chested; withdrawing he asked for death. Five days later the king said: “You have done me no wrong.

sentences.zh: 子為子之臣禮，吾為吾之王禮而已矣。

translations.literal: You perform your rites as minister; I perform my rites as king—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: You keep your rites as minister; I keep mine as king—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」貂勃從楚來，王賜之酒。

translations.literal: ” Diao Bo returned from Chu; the king gave him wine.
translations.idiomatic: ” Diao Bo returned from Chu, and the king gave him wine.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，王曰：「召相單而來！

translations.literal: When the wine was warm, the king said, “Summon Chancellor Dan to come!
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was warm, the king said: “Summon Chancellor Tian Dan!

sentences.zh: 」貂勃避席稽首曰：「王上者孰與周文王？

translations.literal: ” Diao Bo left his mat, bowed head to ground, and said, “Your Majesty above—how do you compare with King Wen of Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: ” Diao Bo left his mat, kowtowed, and said: “Your Majesty above—how do you compare with King Wen of Zhou?

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「吾不若也。

translations.literal: ” The king said, “I do not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king said: “I do not.

sentences.zh: 」貂勃曰：「然，臣固知王不若也。

translations.literal: ” Diao Bo said, “So; your servant always knew Your Majesty did not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Diao Bo said: “So; I always knew Your Majesty did not.

sentences.zh: 下者孰與齊桓公？

translations.literal: Below—how do you compare with Duke Huan of Qi?
translations.idiomatic: Below—how do you compare with Duke Huan of Qi?

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「吾不若也。

translations.literal: ” The king said, “I do not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king said: “I do not.

sentences.zh: 」貂勃曰：「然，臣固知王不若也。

translations.literal: ” Diao Bo said, “So; your servant always knew Your Majesty did not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Diao Bo said: “So; I always knew Your Majesty did not.

sentences.zh: 然則周文王得呂尚以為太公，齊桓公得管夷吾以為仲父，今王得安平君而獨曰『單』，安得此亡國之言乎！

translations.literal: Yet King Wen of Zhou got Lü Shang and made him Grand Duke; Duke Huan of Qi got Guan Yiwu and made him Uncle-Father; now Your Majesty has the Lord of Anping yet alone say ‘Dan’—how can there be such talk of a state's ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Yet King Wen made Lü Shang his Grand Duke, Duke Huan made Guan Yiwu his Uncle-Father—yet Your Majesty has Lord Anping and calls him only ‘Dan’! How can there be such talk of ruin!

sentences.zh: 且自天地之辟，民人之始，為人臣之功者，誰有厚於安平君者哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, from the opening of Heaven and Earth and the beginning of the people, among the achievements of men who served as ministers—who has been thicker than the Lord of Anping?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Heaven and Earth began and men arose, who among ministers has done more than Lord Anping?

sentences.zh: 王不能守王之社稷，燕人興師而襲齊，王走而之城陽之山中，安平君以惴惴即墨三里之城，五里之郭，敝卒七千人，禽其司馬而反千里之齊，安平君之功也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty could not keep your altars; the men of Yan raised troops and struck Qi; Your Majesty fled to the mountains at Chengyang. The Lord of Anping, in fear and trembling, with Jimo's three-li walls and five-li outer works and seven thousand worn troops, captured their marshal and restored a thousand li of Qi—that is the Lord of Anping's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty could not hold the altars; Yan raised troops and struck Qi; you fled to the mountains at Chengyang. Lord Anping, in fear and trembling, with Jimo's three-li walls, five-li suburbs, and seven thousand worn troops, captured their marshal and restored a thousand li of Qi—that is Lord Anping's merit.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，舍城陽而自王，天下莫之能止。

translations.literal: At that time, had he abandoned Chengyang and made himself king, none under Heaven could have stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, had he left Chengyang and made himself king, none under Heaven could have stopped him.

sentences.zh: 然而計之於道，歸之於義，以為不可，故棧道木閣而迎王與后於城陽山中，王乃得反，子臨百姓。

translations.literal: Yet he reckoned by the Way and returned to righteousness, deemed it impossible, and therefore built plank roads and wooden galleries to welcome Your Majesty and the queen from the mountains at Chengyang; only then did Your Majesty return and rule the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he reckoned by the Way and by righteousness, held it wrong, built plank roads and wooden galleries to welcome you and the queen from the Chengyang hills, and only then did you return to rule the people.

sentences.zh: 今國已定，民已安矣，王乃曰『單』，嬰兒之計不為此也。

translations.literal: Now the state is settled and the people are secure—yet Your Majesty says ‘Dan’; no child's plan would do this.
translations.idiomatic: Now the state is settled and the people secure—yet Your Majesty says only ‘Dan’; not even a child's plan would do this.

sentences.zh: 王亟殺此九子者以謝安平君，不然，國其危矣！

translations.literal: Your Majesty should quickly kill these nine men to apologize to the Lord of Anping—otherwise the state will be in peril!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should quickly kill these nine and apologize to Lord Anping—or the state is in peril!

sentences.zh: 」乃殺九子而逐其家，益封安平君以夜邑萬戶<ref>益封安平君以夜邑萬戶「夜邑」，《戰國策》作「掖邑」，班固《漢書》有掖縣，蓋是此地。

translations.literal: ” He then killed the nine men and banished their households, and increased the Lord of Anping's fief by the ten-thousand-household district of Ye<ref>increased the Lord of Anping's fief by the ten-thousand-household district of Ye—“Ye district” in Strategies of the Warring States reads “Ye district” as 掖邑; Ban Gu's Book of Han has Ye county—probably this place.
translations.idiomatic: ” He killed the nine and banished their families, and added to Lord Anping's fief the ten-thousand-household district of Ye<ref>“Ye district” (夜邑)—Strategies of the Warring States has 掖邑; Ban Gu's Book of Han has Ye county—probably this place.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 田單將攻狄，往見魯仲連。

translations.literal: Tian Dan was about to attack Di and went to see Lu Zhonglian.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan was about to attack Di and went to see Lu Zhonglian.

sentences.zh: 魯仲連曰：「將軍攻狄，不能下也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhonglian said, “General, if you attack Di you will not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhonglian said: “General, you will not take Di.

sentences.zh: 」田單曰：「臣以即墨破亡餘卒破萬乘之燕，復齊之墟，今攻狄而不下，何也？

translations.literal: ” Tian Dan said, “Your servant, with Jimo's broken remnant troops, broke ten-thousand-chariot Yan and restored Qi's ruins—now attacking Di and not taking it: why?
translations.idiomatic: ” Tian Dan said: “With Jimo's broken remnant I broke ten-thousand-chariot Yan and restored Qi's lands—why can I not take Di now?

sentences.zh: 」上車弗謝而去，遂攻狄，三月不克。

translations.literal: ” He mounted his carriage without thanking him and left; he then attacked Di, and for three months could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: ” He mounted his carriage without a word of thanks and left; he attacked Di three months without success.

sentences.zh: 齊小兒謠曰：「大冠若箕，修劍拄頤。

translations.literal: The children of Qi sang a rhyme: “Great cap like a winnowing-basket, long sword propping the chin.
translations.idiomatic: The children of Qi sang: “Cap big as a basket, long sword propping his chin.

sentences.zh: 攻狄不能下，壘枯骨成丘。

translations.literal: Attacking Di and not taking it—he piles dry bones into hills.
translations.idiomatic: Cannot take Di—he piles dry bones into hills.

sentences.zh: 」田單乃懼，問魯仲連曰：「先生謂單不能下狄，請問其說。

translations.literal: ” Tian Dan then grew afraid and asked Lu Zhonglian, “The master said Dan could not take Di—may I ask the reason?
translations.idiomatic: ” Tian Dan grew afraid and asked Lu Zhonglian: “You said I could not take Di—may I ask why?

sentences.zh: 」魯仲連曰：「將軍之在即墨，坐則織蕢，立則仗鍤，為士卒倡曰：『無可往矣！

translations.literal: ” Lu Zhonglian said, “When the general was at Jimo, sitting he wove reed mats, standing he leaned on a spade, and for the soldiers led the chant, saying, ‘There is nowhere to go!
translations.idiomatic: ” Lu Zhonglian said, “At Jimo you sat weaving reed mats and stood leaning on a spade, leading the soldiers in a chant: ‘There is nowhere left to go!

sentences.zh: 宗廟亡矣！

translations.literal: The ancestral temples are lost!
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temples are lost!

sentences.zh: 今日尚矣！

translations.literal: Today is the last!
translations.idiomatic: Today is the end!

sentences.zh: 歸於何黨矣！

translations.literal: To which clan shall we return!
translations.idiomatic: To which clan can we return!

sentences.zh: 』當此之時，將軍有死之心，士卒先無之氣，聞君言莫不揮泣奮臂而欲戰，此所以破燕也。

translations.literal: ’ At that time the general had the will to die; the soldiers beforehand lacked such spirit; hearing your words none failed to weep, wave their arms, and wish to fight—this is why Yan was broken.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Then you were ready to die and your men had lost heart; at your words every man wept, raised his arms, and burned to fight—that is how Yan was broken.

sentences.zh: 當今將軍東有夜邑之奉，西有淄上之娛，黃金橫帶而騁乎淄、澠之間，有生之樂，無死之心，所以不勝也。

translations.literal: Now the general has Ye city's revenue in the east and amusements on the Zi in the west, gold across his belt galloping between the Zi and the Mian, the pleasures of life and no will to die—this is why he cannot win.
translations.idiomatic: Now you have Ye's revenues in the east and pleasures on the Zi in the west, gold at your belt, galloping between the Zi and the Mian—the joy of living and no will to die. That is why you cannot win.

sentences.zh: 」田單曰：「單之有心，先生志之矣。

translations.literal: ” Tian Dan said, “Dan's heart—the master has recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tian Dan said, “You have read my heart, sir.

sentences.zh: 」明日，乃厲氣循城，立於矢石之所，援袍鼓之。

translations.literal: ” The next day he stiffened his resolve and went round the wall, stood where arrows and stones fell, took cloak and drumstick and beat the drum.
translations.idiomatic: ” Next day he roused his spirit, circled the wall, stood where arrows and stones fell, and beat the war drum.

sentences.zh: 狄人乃下。

translations.literal: The Di then came down.
translations.idiomatic: The Di then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，齊湣王既滅宋，欲去孟嘗君。

translations.literal: Earlier, after King Min of Qi had destroyed Song, he wished to remove Lord Mengchang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after King Min of Qi destroyed Song, he wished to remove Lord Mengchang.

sentences.zh: 孟嘗君奔魏，魏昭王以為相，與諸侯共伐破齊。

translations.literal: Lord Mengchang fled to Wei; King Zhao of Wei made him chancellor, and with the feudal lords together attacked and broke Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang fled to Wei. King Zhao of Wei made him chancellor, and with the other lords he helped smash Qi.

sentences.zh: 湣王死，襄王復國，而孟嘗君中立為諸侯，無所屬。

translations.literal: King Min died; King Xiang restored the state, while Lord Mengchang stood neutral as a feudal lord, belonging to none.
translations.idiomatic: King Min died. King Xiang restored Qi, while Lord Mengchang held himself neutral among the lords, belonging to no one.

sentences.zh: 襄王新立，畏孟嘗君，與之連和。

translations.literal: King Xiang had newly succeeded and feared Lord Mengchang; he joined in alliance with him.
translations.idiomatic: The newly enthroned King Xiang feared Lord Mengchang and allied with him.

sentences.zh: 孟嘗君卒，諸子爭立，而齊、魏共滅薛，孟嘗君絕嗣。

translations.literal: Lord Mengchang died; his sons contended for succession, and Qi and Wei together destroyed Xue—Lord Mengchang's line ended.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang died. His sons fought over the succession; Qi and Wei together destroyed Xue, and his line died out.

translations.literal: Lord Wu'an again fought Zhao's general Jia Yan and sank twenty thousand of his soldiers in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Wu'an again fought Zhao's general Jia Yan and drowned twenty thousand of his men in the river.

sentences.zh: 魏段干子請割南陽予秦以和。

translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Duan Ganzi to offer Nanyang to Qin for peace.

translations.literal: the one who wants the land is Qin.

sentences.zh: 今王使欲地者制璽，欲璽者制地，魏地盡矣！

translations.literal: Now if Your Majesty lets the one who wants land control the seal and the one who wants the seal control the land, Wei's territory will be exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: Now you let the one who wants land control the seal and the one who wants the seal control the land—Wei will lose everything!

sentences.zh: 夫以地事秦，猶抱薪救火，薪不盡，火不滅。

translations.literal: Serving Qin with land is like carrying firewood to put out a fire—as long as the firewood is not exhausted, the fire is not extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Feeding Qin with land is like carrying firewood to a fire—as long as the wood lasts, the fire will not die.

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty use wisdom less well than using the owl?
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty use less sense than an owl token?

sentences.zh: 2韓釐王薨，子桓惠王立。

translations.literal: 2 King Xi of Han died; his son King Huanhui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: 2 King Xi of Han died; his son King Huanhui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 致至則危，累棋是也。

translations.literal: when piled to the limit they become perilous—stacked chess pieces are so.
translations.idiomatic: when piled to the limit they topple—stacked chess pieces are so.

sentences.zh: 今大國之地，遍天下有其二垂，此從生民已來，萬乘之地未嘗有也。

translations.literal: Now the great state's territory spans the world and holds two of its quarters; since the birth of the people, a realm of ten thousand chariots has never had the like.
translations.idiomatic: Your great state's lands now span the world and hold two of its quarters—since mankind began, no realm of ten thousand chariots has ever held so much.

sentences.zh: 先王三世不忘接地於齊，以絕從親之要。

translations.literal: For three generations the former kings never forgot to join territory with Qi, to cut off the vital point of horizontal alliances.
translations.idiomatic: For three generations your forebears never ceased pressing against Qi, to sever the throat of horizontal alliances.

sentences.zh: 今王使盛橋守事於韓，盛橋以其地入秦，是王不用甲，不信威，而得百里之地，王可謂能矣！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty sent Sheng Qiao to hold affairs in Han, and Sheng Qiao brought his territory into Qin—Your Majesty used no armor, relied on no mere show of force, and gained a hundred li of land; Your Majesty may be called capable!
translations.idiomatic: You sent Sheng Qiao to hold affairs in Han, and he brought his territory into Qin—you used no armor, no empty threat, and gained a hundred li of land. You may be called capable!

sentences.zh: 王又舉甲而攻魏，杜大樑之門，舉河內，拔燕、酸棗、虛、桃，入邢，魏之兵雲翔而不敢救，王之功亦多矣！

translations.literal: Your Majesty again raised armor and attacked Wei, shut the gates of Daliang, took Henei, seized Yan, Suanzao, Xu, and Tao, entered Xing—Wei's troops clouded the sky yet dared not rescue; Your Majesty's achievements are many!
translations.idiomatic: You again raised armies against Wei, shut Daliang's gates, took Henei, seized Yan, Suanzao, Xu, and Tao, entered Xing—Wei's troops swarmed like clouds yet dared not rescue. Your achievements are many!

sentences.zh: 王休甲息眾，二年而後復之，又並蒲、衍、首、垣以臨仁、平丘，黃、濟陽嬰城而魏氏服。

translations.literal: Your Majesty rested armor and eased the masses; after two years you resumed, again united Pu, Yan, Shou, and Yuan to overlook Ren and Pingqiu—Huang and Jiyang held their walls tight and Wei submitted.
translations.idiomatic: You rested your armies and eased your people; two years later you resumed, united Pu, Yan, Shou, and Yuan to overlook Ren and Pingqiu, and with Huang and Jiyang walled tight Wei submitted.

sentences.zh: 王又割濮磨之北，注齊、秦之要，絕楚、趙之脊，天下五合六聚而不敢救，王之威亦單矣！

translations.literal: Your Majesty again cut north of Pu and Mo, poured into the vital points of Qi and Qin, severed the spine of Chu and Zhao—the world five times united and six times gathered yet dared not rescue; Your Majesty's majesty stands alone!
translations.idiomatic: You again cut north of Pu and Mo, struck at Qi and Qin's vital points, severed Chu and Zhao's spine—the world united again and again yet dared not rescue. Your majesty stands alone!

sentences.zh: 王若能保功守威，絀攻取之心，而肥仁義之地，使無後患，三王不足四，五伯不足六也！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can preserve achievement and guard majesty, restrain the heart of attack and seizure, and enrich the ground of benevolence and righteousness so there are no later troubles, the Three Kings are not enough for a fourth, the Five Hegemons not enough for a sixth!
translations.idiomatic: If you can preserve your gains and guard your prestige, curb the urge to seize, and enrich the ground of benevolence and righteousness so there are no later troubles, you will outdo the Three Kings and surpass the Five Hegemons!

sentences.zh: 王若負人徒之眾，仗兵革之強，乘毀魏之威，而欲以力臣天下之主，臣恐其有後患也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty relies on the multitude of men and followers, trusts in the strength of arms, rides the prestige of destroying Wei, and wishes by force to make the world's lords your subjects, your servant fears there will be later troubles.
translations.idiomatic: If you rely on your masses, trust in arms, ride the prestige of crushing Wei, and mean to force the world's lords into subjection, I fear later troubles.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：『靡不有初，鮮克有終。

translations.literal: The Odes say: ‘There is nothing without a beginning; few reach the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: ‘Nothing lacks a beginning; few reach the end.

translations.idiomatic: ’ This means beginnings are easy and endings hard.

sentences.zh: 昔吳之信越也，從而伐齊，既勝齊人於艾陵，還為越禽於三江之浦。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu trusted Yue and followed them to attack Qi; having defeated the men of Qi at Ailing, on return Wu was taken by Yue at the mouth of the Three Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu trusted Yue, followed them against Qi, defeated Qi at Ailing, and on the way home was captured by Yue at the mouth of the Three Rivers.

sentences.zh: 智氏之信韓、魏也，從而伐趙，攻晉陽城，勝有日矣，韓、魏叛之，殺智伯瑤於鑿台之下。

translations.literal: The house of Zhi trusted Han and Wei and followed them to attack Zhao; they besieged Jinyang, victory was near, Han and Wei rebelled, and killed Zhi Bo Yao below the Zao Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Zhi trusted Han and Wei, followed them against Zhao, besieged Jinyang with victory near, then Han and Wei rebelled and killed Zhi Bo Yao below the Zao Terrace.

sentences.zh: 今王妒楚之不毀，而忘毀楚之強韓、魏也，臣為王慮而不取也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty resents that Chu is not destroyed, yet forgets that destroying Chu strengthens Han and Wei—your servant counsels Your Majesty not to take this course.
translations.idiomatic: You resent that Chu is not destroyed, yet forget that destroying Chu strengthens Han and Wei. I urge you not to take this course.

sentences.zh: 夫楚國，援也；

translations.literal: Chu is a support;
translations.idiomatic: Chu is a support;

sentences.zh: 鄰國，敵也。

translations.literal: neighboring states are enemies.
translations.idiomatic: neighboring states are enemies.

sentences.zh: 今王信韓、魏之善王，此正吳之信越也，臣恐韓、魏卑辭除患而實欲欺大國也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty trusts Han and Wei's goodwill toward you—this is exactly Wu trusting Yue; your servant fears Han and Wei with humble words remove trouble but in truth wish to deceive the great state.
translations.idiomatic: You trust Han and Wei's goodwill—this is Wu trusting Yue again. I fear they speak humbly to remove danger but in truth mean to deceive your great state.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 王無重世之德於韓、魏而有累世之怨焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has no virtue piled over generations toward Han and Wei, but grudges piled over generations.
translations.idiomatic: You have heaped no kindness on Han and Wei over generations, but heaped grudges over generations.

translations.literal: Now if Your Majesty supplies them to attack Chu, is that not excessive!
translations.idiomatic: Now to arm them to attack Chu—is that not going too far!

sentences.zh: 且攻楚將惡出兵？

translations.literal: Moreover, attacking Chu—how will you send troops?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, attacking Chu—how will you march?

sentences.zh: 王將借路於仇讎之韓、魏乎？

translations.literal: Will Your Majesty borrow a route through Han and Wei, your mortal foes?
translations.idiomatic: Will you borrow a route through Han and Wei, your mortal foes?

sentences.zh: 兵出之日而王憂其不反也。

translations.literal: The day the army marches forth Your Majesty will worry that it does not return.
translations.idiomatic: The day your army marches out you will fear it will not return.

sentences.zh: 王若不借路於仇讎之韓、魏，必攻隨水右壤，此皆廣川、大水、山林、溪谷，不食之地。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not borrow a route through Han and Wei, your foes, you must attack the right bank of the Sui—all broad rivers, great waters, mountains, forests, ravines, and gorges, lands that yield no food.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not borrow a route through Han and Wei, your foes, you must attack the right bank of the Sui—all broad rivers, great floods, mountains, forests, and ravines, lands that yield no food.

sentences.zh: 是王有毀楚之名而無得地之實也。

translations.literal: Then Your Majesty will have the name of destroying Chu but not the reality of gaining land.
translations.idiomatic: Then you will earn the name of destroying Chu but gain no land.

sentences.zh: 且王攻楚之日，四國必悉起兵以應王。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the day Your Majesty attacks Chu, the four states will surely all raise troops to respond to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the day you attack Chu, the four states will surely all raise troops against you.

sentences.zh: 秦、楚之兵構而不離；

translations.literal: Qin and Chu's armies will be locked and not part;
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Chu will be locked in battle and unable to break off;

sentences.zh: 魏氏將出而攻留、方輿、銍、湖陵、碭、蕭、相，故宋必盡；

translations.literal: Wei will march out and attack Liu, Fangyu, Zhi, Huling, Dang, Xiao, and Xiang—the old lands of Song will all be gone;
translations.idiomatic: Wei will march out against Liu, Fangyu, Zhi, Huling, Dang, Xiao, and Xiang—the old lands of Song will all be lost;

sentences.zh: 齊人南面攻楚，泗上必舉。

translations.literal: the men of Qi will attack Chu from the south; the lands above the Si will surely fall.
translations.idiomatic: Qi will attack Chu from the north; the lands above the Si will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 此皆平原四達膏腴之地。

translations.literal: These are all level plains open on four sides, rich and fertile lands.
translations.idiomatic: These are all level plains with roads in every direction, rich and fertile country.

sentences.zh: 如此，則天下之國莫強於齊、魏矣。

translations.literal: If so, then among states under Heaven none will be stronger than Qi and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: If things go thus, then among the states of the world none will be stronger than Qi and Wei.

sentences.zh: 臣為王慮，莫若善楚。

translations.literal: Your servant has considered for Your Majesty: nothing is better than treating Chu well.
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed matters for Your Majesty: you had best befriend Chu.

sentences.zh: 秦、楚合而為一以臨韓，韓必斂手而朝；

translations.literal: If Qin and Chu unite as one to face Han, Han will surely fold its hands and pay court;
translations.idiomatic: If Qin and Chu unite and press Han, Han will surely fold its hands and submit;

sentences.zh: 王施以東山之險，帶以曲河之利，韓必為關內之侯。

translations.literal: Your Majesty deploying the danger of the eastern hills, girding with the advantage of the winding rivers, Han will surely become a marquis within the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy the heights of the eastern hills and bind them with the advantage of the winding rivers, and Han will surely become a marquis of the inner domain.

sentences.zh: 若是而王以十萬戍鄭，梁氏寒心，許、鄢陵嬰城而上蔡、召陵不往來也。

translations.literal: If so, and Your Majesty garrisons Zheng with a hundred thousand, the house of Liang will lose heart; Xu and Yanling will wall their cities; and Shangcai and Shaoling will have no coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Then, if Your Majesty stations a hundred thousand at Zheng, Wei will lose heart; Xu and Yanling will shut their walls; Shangcai and Shaoling will cease their traffic.

sentences.zh: 如此，魏亦關內侯矣。

translations.literal: If so, Wei too will be a marquis within the pass.
translations.idiomatic: If so, Wei too will be a marquis of the inner domain.

sentences.zh: 王壹善楚而關內兩萬乘之主注地於齊，齊右壤可拱手而取也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty befriends Chu in one stroke and the two lords of ten thousand chariots within the pass pour territory toward Qi, Qi's right lands can be taken with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: Befriend Chu outright, and when the two ten-thousand-chariot lords within the pass turn their lands toward Qi, you can take Qi's right flank with folded hands.

sentences.zh: 王之地一經兩海，要約天下，是燕、趙無齊、楚，齊、楚無燕、趙也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's lands running through both seas, binding the world under key terms—Yan and Zhao will lack Qi and Chu, Qi and Chu will lack Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Your lands will span both seas and bind the world by strategic holds; Yan and Zhao will lack Qi and Chu, and Qi and Chu will lack Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 然後危動燕、趙，直搖齊、楚，此四國者不待痛而服矣。

translations.literal: Then threaten and stir Yan and Zhao, shake Qi and Chu directly—these four states will submit without being wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Then alarm Yan and Zhao and shake Qi and Chu directly—these four states will yield without your needing to wound them.

sentences.zh: 」王從之，止武安君而謝韓、魏，使黃歇歸，約親於楚。

translations.literal: ” The king followed this, stopped the Lord of Wu'an and apologized to Han and Wei, sent Huang Xie home, and pledged kinship with Chu.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king accepted this, held back the Lord of Wu'an and made apology to Han and Wei, sent Huang Xie home, and pledged alliance with Chu.

translations.literal: Zhou
translations.idiomatic: Zhou
